articles.title: Unemployment eases to 5.3% in August 2026 as agriculture adds jobs
articles.summary: Manufacturing continues to weaken as employment in the sector further fell to 3.16 million in August from 3.43 million in July

blocks.text: UPLAND. Farmers harvest potatoes at a farm in Atok, Benguet, on March 31, 2026.
Manufacturing continues to weaken as employment in the sector further fell to 3.16 million in August from 3.43 million in July

items: The unemployment rate in the Philippines decreased to 5.3% in August 2026.
Employment gains were primarily seen in agriculture and forestry, while manufacturing continued to decline.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines’ unemployment rate eased to 5.3% in August 2026 as more Filipinos found work, particularly in the agriculture sector.
Around 2.77 million Filipinos were unemployed in August, down from 3.14 million in July, according to preliminary data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).

The unemployment rate likewise fell from 6% in July, when it hit its highest level in more than four years. However, the August figure is worse than the 3.9% unemployment rate recorded in the same month of 2025.
National Statistician Dennis Mapa said the improvement from July was partly because fewer new entrants joined the labor force after the surge of fresh graduates looking for jobs the previous month.

Around 897,000 Filipinos joined the labor force for the first time in August, down from 1.5 million in July. Of these new entrants, around 470,000 were employed while 427,000 were unemployed, according to Mapa.

Agriculture and forestry accounted for the biggest month-on-month increase in employment, adding around 847,000 workers. Construction added another 390,000 jobs, while wholesale and retail trade gained 227,000.
Mapa said much of the agriculture increase came from rice and sugarcane production.

Manufacturing, however, continued to weaken. Employment in the sector fell to 3.16 million in August from 3.43 million in July and 3.46 million in June. Mapa said the electronics industry was among those affected, citing challenges in the global market, although seasonality may also be a factor.

blocks.caption: [READOUT] Where businesses can plug into the Luzon Corridor

blocks.text: Underemployment also improved month-on-month, falling to 11.9% in August from 12.9% in July. This meant around 5.9 million employed Filipinos still wanted additional working hours or another job. The rate, however, was higher than the 10.7% recorded in August 2025.

Bad weather also affected the quality of work during the month. Average hours worked fell to 39.2 hours a week from 40.6 hours in July, with millions of workers reporting bad weather as a reason for working fewer hours.
Mapa said shorter working hours could also translate to lower incomes for some workers, particularly the self-employed and those paid according to the amount of time they work.
The PSA expects employment to pick up toward the end of the year as businesses hire more seasonal workers ahead of the Christmas period. – Rappler.com

articles.title: NBI to coordinate with BI for Velasco's whereabouts
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation on Wednesday said it will coordinate with the Bureau of Immigration (BI) to determine the whereabouts of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.

blocks.text: Published October 7, 2026 10:11am
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday said it will coordinate with the Bureau of Immigration (BI) to determine the whereabouts of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Interviewed on GMA News’ Unang Balita, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said immigration records show that Velasco traveled to Japan.
“Well, as far as the records of Immigration, ang kanya pong records nagsabi na sa Japan nagtungo. Sa ngayon po kasi siya hindi naman isang government official,” he said.
(Well, as far as the records of Immigration, his records say that he went to Japan. At the moment, he is not a government official.)

“Kaya medyo mas ang ating pag-verify niyan sa private citizen ay sa BI lamang po. So tingnan po natin at ipapa-check natin sa Immigration kung meron pong mga naging connecting flight or umalis po or kung nasa Japan pa rin po,” he added.
(So our verification for private citizens is through BI only. So let's see and have Immigration check if there were any connecting flights or if he left or if he is still in Japan.)
The BI said last September 29 that Velasco was out of the country, saying there is no derogatory record preventing his departure from the country.
It also said that there is no existing hold departure order against Velasco.

Velasco's former security aide Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. earlier claimed that he delivered suitcases containing over P2 billion in cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, her father former President Rodrigo Duterte, and her brother Davao City Representative Paolo "Pulong" Duterte.
The ex-cop said he was ordered by Velasco.
Velasco’s camp however said that the allegations have “no basis” and are “fabricated attacks” against him.

"The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested," said Velasco's spokesperson, Atty. Rowell Ilagan in a statement.
Velasco's camp also called the accusations against the former speaker as "inconsistent."

Ilagan, who appeared before the NBI on Monday to answer its invite to Velasco, said they will answer all the allegations against the former House speaker once they have reviewed the documents, adding that they only formally received the affidavit of Gracioso that day.
For her part, VP Sara said she does not know Gracioso and did not receive money from him.
The vice president, in a press conference on Tuesday, denied the allegation and said Gracioso was motivated by money and resentment towards Velasco and his family.
According to the vice president, President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and his administration are behind the allegations against her.
Malacañang on Tuesday however said that if VP Sara Duterte answered allegations against her "clearly," then perhaps there would be no impeachment trial.
Duterte's camp has yet to provide evidence to counter Gracioso's claims, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said.
Matibag on Tuesday said Sara Duterte's denial of allegations made by Gracioso should be formally submitted under oath.

Former presidential spokesperson Salvador Panelo earlier said the claim that suitcases containing cash were delivered to the Duterte family is a “fabricated story” to oust and disqualify VP Sara Duterte in the 2028 elections. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Friends of Nolan Wells sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation
articles.summary:
Owens sued over September Instagram post that suggested trio tampered with evidence in death of Mississippi teen

Three friends of

blocks.text: Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Mississippi teen who died after a July boating trip, have sued NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

On 26 September, Owens shared an Instagram video that suggested Wells’s friends Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour had deleted evidence from Wells’s phone after his death, which the three men denied in their lawsuit.
“Arrest them immediately!! Like yesterday,” Owens captioned the post.

In a Monday complaint filed in a Mississippi district court, the fathers of the three young men, who are also named in the complaint as plaintiffs because they are deemed minors under state law, accuse Owens of harming their reputation and endangering their physical safety with the post.

“Due to the conduct of Owens and many other less-famous individuals, these completely innocent young men have been subjected to thousands of death threats, face-to-face harassment, and daily fear and ridicule from complete strangers. They’ve even been refused service at public establishments. Their lives, and the lives of their family members, will never be the same,” the complaint alleges.
Owens could not be immediately reached for comment.
The friends’ counsel also indicated they intend to take legal action against other public figures who have been vocal about Wells’s death including Al Sharpton and The View’s Sunny Hostin.
On 4 July, Wells and his friends sailed for a Mississippi island. He was last seen that afternoon. Two days later, his body was found on the island.

The circumstances of his death have fueled public suspicion. Wells, who was African American, had been partying with a mostly white friend group – a detail that gained traction online as some referenced Mississippi’s past with racial violence.

In late September, a Mississippi grand jury declined to file criminal charges, finding Wells’s death to appear “consistent with drowning”. Jackson county district attorney Angel Myers McIlrath has said Wells’s death was not racially motivated.

Wells’s parents and civil rights lawyer Ben Crump continue to call for further investigations, citing the state’s autopsy report, which said Wells’s airways and stomach were empty. His family has said the lack of water found undermines the drowning determination.

“I cannot take that ruling, and I cannot move on with my life,” Christine Wonsley, Wells’s mother, reportedly said, referring to the grand jury’s findings at a Monday press conference. “We have been left with more questions and heartbreak than any answers.”

MANILA, Philippines – Agnés Callamard, barred from setting foot in the Philippines by former president Rodrigo Duterte in 2018, returns to the Philippines for the first time to address an urgent global issue: how can we protect human rights and democracies from the threats posed by unregulated artificial intelligence (AI)?

Callamard, in her capacity as United Nations special rapporteur for extrajudicial killings during the Duterte presidency, had been outspoken about the conduct of his drug war, angering Duterte enough to ban her from the country.
In September this year, the Bureau of Immigration lifted the ban, paving the way for Callamard to return to the Philippines to speak at Rappler’s Social Good Summit 2026 happening on November 21.

Callamard, now secretary general of international human rights watchdog organization Amnesty International, will speak about the impact of artificial intelligence on human rights and basic freedoms at the summit.

Entitled, “WE THE HUMANS: Reclaim Our Future,” this year’s summit focuses on what humanity can still do to protect human values, human creativity, and human communities from the threats posed by unregulated and abused AI systems.

In recent months, rogue AI agents and words of warning coming even from the leaders of major AI companies and tech tycoons, point to an urgent need for humanity to come together to rein in AI development and protect human communities.

Without the proper guard rails, AI models pose an existential threat to humanity, supercharging wars and disinformation, compounding isolation, undermining critical thinking and learning abilities, and more.

The Social Good Summit is Rappler’s biggest annual fundraising event, with proceeds going to its investigative journalism and AI literacy initiatives. The summit will happen on November 21 at Shangri-La The Fort, Manila. Other speakers include AI Singapore’s Leslie Teo (also a member of the UN scientific panel on AI), historian Yuval Noah Harari (virtual), Rappler CEO and 2021 Nobel laureate Maria Ressa, and more. (READ: Learn, connect, be human: Social Good Summit unveils AI masterclasses)

Callamard is uniquely placed to speak about the global outlook of human rights, in the face of rapid AI development. She has led human rights investigations in over 30 countries, including the investigations into the murder of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi. She has studied and written about women’s rights, freedom of expression, refugee movements, arbitrary killings, and more.

At Columbia University, she was director of the Global Freedom of Expression Project. She also served as executive director of the Freedom of Expression organization ARTICLE 19 and HAP International (the Humanitarian Accountability Partnership).

As secretary general of Amnesty International, she serves as its principal spokesperson. Amnesty International, one of the world’s largest non-governmental human rights organizations, has around 10 million supporters and offices in over 70 countries.

While she was UN rapporteur for extrajudicial killings, then-president Rodrigo Duterte threatened to slap her for “insulting” him with her words about his controversial anti-illegal drugs campaign. The Philippines’ own Commission on Human Rights said the president’s expletives and threats had a chilling effect on human rights defenders.

Today, Duterte is detained by the International Criminal Court in the Hague, Netherlands to stand trial for alleged crimes against humanity. His full-blown trial is set to begin on November 30. His anti-illegal drugs campaign resulted in at least 6,200 deaths in police operations alone by May 2022. articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute.

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump, left, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are seen in Alaska in August 2025. (Jae C. Hong/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute.
WHO says Siberia case presents a 'very low' risk outside Russia

Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said he would be talking with Putin about the case "very soon." Health authorities are investigating after the death of an employee at an anti-plague institute, which authorities attributed to pneumonia with an unknown cause.

Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Trump said the U.S. is in "very deep discussions" on the topic. "We'll be able to report about it, probably tomorrow," Trump said.

The World Health Organization on Tuesday said the case presents a "very low" risk outside Russia. The United Nations agency said it was in contact with Russian authorities following reports of the death last week of a woman who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.
On Monday, Trump said the U.S. would be willing to help Russia with the situation.
What we know about the suspected plague death in Russia

The call also comes as the Trump administration faces an Oct. 18 deadline to decide which Russian entities, if any, it will sanction under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Trump signed into law on Sept. 18.
Ukraine has given the administration and Congress a wish list of Russian companies, vessels and individuals it would like to see hit with U.S. sanctions under that law.

articles.title: OCD: Nearly P11B worth of assistance given to El Niño-hit farmers
articles.summary: The government has provided P10.96 billion in interventions and assistance to farmers affected by the effects of the El Niño phenomenon, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published October 7, 2026 9:44am
The government has provided P10.96 billion in interventions and assistance to farmers affected by the effects of the El Niño phenomenon, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Wednesday.
Interviewed on GMA News’ Unang Balita, OCD spokesperson Junie Castillo said the aid is part of the government's efforts to protect food security amid drought conditions.

“Ito po ay umaabot na sa P10.96 billion po 'yung mga intervention o assistance na ibinibigay natin sa mga kababayan nating mga magsasaka. Ito naman ay through the crop insurance, mga production assistance, ganun din sa patubig nila,” he said.
(The total interventions or assistance we are providing to our farmers reached P10.96 billion. Whether it is through crop insurance, production assistance, or even their irrigation.)
Castillo said the Department of Agriculture (DA) is leading the government's food security efforts under the National Action Plan on El Niño.
The latest report showed that 106 cities and municipalities have declared a state of calamity due to the effects of El Niño.
The affected areas include parts of Cagayan Valley, Calabarzon, Bicol, SOCCSKSARGEN, and Caraga.
Among the provinces with state of calamity declarations are Isabela, Cagayan, Camarines Norte, Dinagat Islands, and Agusan del Sur.
DA has reported about P6.87 billion in agricultural losses and damage, with around 249,000 hectares of crops affected.
Castillo said the government is helping farmers determine which crops are suitable under the prevailing conditions to help ensure the continuous supply of food.
Cloud-seeding operations are being implemented in affected areas.
The OCD also emphasized the need for water conservation amid the El Niño impact. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Not exactly his favorite senator’: Susan Collins distances herself from Trump in Maine debate
articles.summary:
Republican challenged by Democrat Troy Jackson in critical Senate race says she opposes Iran war and Canada tariffs

Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced…

blocks.text: Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced herself from Donald Trump in a televised debate with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson on Tuesday, as she sought to present an image of independence in a state that has voted against Trump three times.

Proclaiming herself as not the US president’s “favorite senator”, Collins made the highly unusual boast for a Republican that she had voted with Joe Biden, a Democrat, more than 90% of the time when he was president. She also emphasized her differences with her fellow Republicans, saying she voted against her own party more than any other senator.

Collins’ defensiveness came amid a determined onslaught from Jackson, 58, a veteran former state legislator who was getting his first chance to present himself to a broad audience since replacing Graham Platner as the Democratic candidate in a contest that could be vital to the party’s hopes of winning the Senate.

Platner, a former harbor master, was forced to withdraw from the race in July after facing sexual assault allegations, which he denied, leaving Democrats racing against the clock to replace a candidate who had built up momentum campaigning on a populist progressive platform.

Jackson painted Collins as a Trump loyalist, saying she voted with the president 96% of the time. He also doggedly focused on her 2018 vote for the conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh, tying it to the court’s subsequent overturning of Roe v Wade, which had for half a century guaranteed the national right to abortion.

“Tonight is about who you stand with when it matters,” Jackson said in a pithy opening statement. “Eight years ago today, Maine women went to DC and begged Senator Collins not to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, but she did it anyways.
“He helped overturn Roe v Wade, and today she says she has no regrets. Would you trust her to pick the next supreme court justice?”

Collins, 73, who has been a senator since 1996, has frequently presented herself as a moderate who stands against more radical trends in her own party. The posture is in line with Maine’s profile as a more Democratic-leaning state, which Trump has not won in any of his three presidential campaigns and which has voted for Democrat presidential candidates in every election since 1992.

Nevertheless, Collins went to unusual lengths to differentiate herself from Trump on a range of issues, including the war with Iran, which she said she voted to end nine times, calling it “not well thought out”.
Collins reacted with something close to alarm when the moderator, Gregg Lagerquist, said Trump had suggested that the president might pay a campaign visit to Maine.

“I don’t think that President Trump is going to come to Maine,” she said. “He’s talking about going to a lot of different states. I’ve heard nothing from his office, and I’m not exactly his favorite senator.”
Collins stressed her differences with the president on specific issues pertinent to the Maine economy, including rural healthcare and tariffs against Canada, with which the state shares a border.
“I have been the most outspoken opponent of the tariffs on Canada,” she said. “Canada is not China. It’s our neighbor and our friends.”
Polls show the two candidates running neck and neck.

blocks.text: FORUM. Batangas 1st District Representative Leandro Leviste answers questions and issues raised by journalists during the Kapihan ng Samahang Plaridel in Manila on May 22, 2026.
Rappler
Leviste faces a warrant over alleged violation of the Public Service Act. The bail is set at P72,000.
MANILA, Philippines – A Makati City court ordered the arrest of Batangas 1st District Representative Leandro Leviste over alleged violation of the Public Service Act.

“You are hereby commanded to arrest Leandro Antonio Leviste, who is/are said to be found in/at N/A… Calatagan, Batangas, Calabarzon or elsewhere, and who has/have been charged before me with the offense of Public Service Act (Section 25 of Commonwealth Act No. 146, as amended by Republic Act No. 11659) and bring him/her/them forthwith before me to be dealt with according to law,” the warrant issued by Makati City Regional Trial Court Branch 235 Presiding Judge Ricardo Moldez II states.
The bail is set at P72,000.
The Public Services Act, among others, provides for the proper regulation of public services like electricity.

Section 25 of the law punishes individuals or organizations, if found guilty, with a fine not exceeding P2 million and/or by jail time of not lower than six years and one day, but not higher than 12 years.
Leviste and his mother, Senator Loren Legarda, have been overseas since August, according to the Bureau of Immigration. Legarda is on medical leave until October 9.

News of the mother and son’s departure came days after Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla announced that different legal actions – plunder and graft complaints – are currently pending against Legarda and Leviste over the latter’s solar energy projects. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Climate summit calls for stronger action to curb global warming
articles.summary: 'As global temperature increases approach 1.5C and we face strong El Nino conditions, we reiterate that every fraction of a degree of warming accelerates the impacts of climate change and increases…

blocks.text: DROUGHT. This file photo shows a view of cracked ground at a dam, as Zimbabwe is experiencing an El Niño-induced drought, resulting in malnutrition among children under the age of five, pregnant and lactating women, and adolescents, in Mudzi, Zimbabwe, on July 2, 2024.
Philimon Bulawayo/Reuters

'As global temperature increases approach 1.5C and we face strong El Nino conditions, we reiterate that every fraction of a degree of warming accelerates the impacts of climate change and increases the risk of irreversible loss and damage for climate vulnerable communities,' ministers say ahead of the UN's COP31 summit

Countries must urgently scale up their commitments to keep temperature rises within 1.5 degrees Celsius to limit the impacts of extreme weather, a statement from a conference leading up to the UN’s COP31 summit said.

The ministerial meeting, being held in Fiji and Tuvalu, said on Tuesday, October 6, that “deep, rapid and sustained emissions reductions are required to minimise the magnitude and duration of overshoot” of the target.

“As global temperature increases approach 1.5C and we face strong El Nino conditions, we reiterate that every fraction of a degree of warming accelerates the impacts of climate change and increases the risk of irreversible loss and damage for climate vulnerable communities,” the statement said.
Some Pacific nations face an existential threat from rising sea levels driven by climate change.
Tuvalu’s sea levels have risen about 15 cm (6 inches) in the three decades to 2023, according to NASA researchers, twice as fast as the global average.

Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, governments committed to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial period, a threshold the UN’s environmental body warned last month the world would exceed “within a few years.”

The pre-COP31 conference also reaffirmed the importance of continuing sovereignty and the rights of states to maintain maritime zones under international law, even as climate-related sea-level rise threatens to reshape coastlines in the Pacific.
Pre-COP events, preparatory meetings leading up to the United Nations COP31 climate forum in Turkey in November, are typically technocratic meetings of climate negotiators.

Australia and Pacific partners are working together through the COP31 Pacific Partnership to ensure Pacific voices and solutions are at the center of global climate action, while also seeking to strengthen regional ties ahead of the main summit. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Comedian Dave Hughes to stop speaking at Liberal party events over political donation concerns
articles.summary:
Entertainer alleges complaint made about ‘in-kind’ donations over Victorian fundraisers, where he has been railing against Labor

  • Get our

blocks.text: Dave Hughes says he will no longer be taking the stage at Victorian Liberal events, claiming the party decided having him on the bill could run afoul of the state’s political donation laws.

The comedian, better known as Hughesy, once described himself as a lifelong Labor voter, but has become a vocal critic of the party following May’s federal budget, which included sweeping reforms to negative gearing and capital gain tax concessions.
He has since been campaigning for the Liberals ahead of the November Victorian election.

This includes headlining the party’s western Victoria region campaign launch in Geelong – a free event held on 16 August – and two fundraisers: a $2,500-per-head dinner on 10 September for its Bentleigh candidate, Tynan Putt; and a $30 “Pub Talk” alongside the Williamstown candidate, Paul Lindemann, on 16 September.
In a video posted to his social media accounts on Tuesday, Hughes said was no longer able to speak at such events after a report to the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC).
“Apparently because of what I would normally charge, that’s above the donation limit,” he said.
“I’ve said I’m not taking any money for political speaking, so I can’t do any more talks at Liberal events.”

On X, Hughes alleged that Victorian Labor had made the VEC complaint. However a senior Labor source said they were not involved. The Age, which first reported the story, reported that the complaint was made by a Labor supporter.

Under Victoria’s donation laws, providing a service for free or below market value is treated as an in-kind political donation and is subject to the same rules as cash donations, which are capped at $5,190.

The VEC’s donations disclosure register shows in-kind services alongside cash donations. It shows that comedian and Greens member Tom Ballard appeared at a party fundraiser in March, with the value of his service recorded as $1,200.
after newsletter promotion
Hughes claimed while Labor had the “massive union movement behind them”, most Liberal candidates “don’t have money behind them” and were “struggling like every other Victorian”.
“So that’s why I want to help them out,” he said.
The VEC donations register shows the Liberals have received $173,222 in donations this financial year, compared to Labor’s $775,264.
The Victorian Liberal party has been approached for comment.

articles.title: NBI's Matibag: Sara Duterte's denial of Gracioso's claims should be under oath

blocks.text: Published October 7, 2026 9:14am

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday said Vice President Sara Duterte's denial of allegations made by former police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. should be formally submitted under oath.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag said Duterte's statements during a press conference could be submitted to investigators.

“Wala pong pasabi, except kahapon nakita natin na nag-press con po. May binabasa siyang papel, kaya maaaring 'yun po 'yung affidavit niya, kaya baka isusumite po sa atin. So hintayin na lang po natin kung ano po 'yung magiging aksyon niya,” he said in an interview on Unang Balita.

(There is no word except yesterday we saw her hold a press conference; she was reading a paper, so it could be her affidavit, so maybe it will be submitted to us. So let's just wait and see what her actions will be.)

“Pero may mga pagsasalita na siya na tinatangging mga salita doon po sa press conference. 'Yun nga lamang po, siyempre 'yung ganyan po dapat under oath din po ginagawa para magkaroon po ng force of law or effect ng law po sa ating pong pagsisiyasat,” he added.
(But she has already made some statements of denial in the press conference. But of course, that should be done under oath so that it has the force of law or the effect of law in our investigation.)

NBI earlier invited Duterte in connection with the claims of Gracioso that he delivered suitcases containing over P2 billion in cash to the Vice President, her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and her brother, Representative Paolo Duterte.
Gracioso, who served as former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco’s security aide, said he did it upon the instruction of the latter.
At a press conference on Tuesday, Duterte denied claims made by Gracioso and said that she will submit an affidavit on Thursday.
“Mariin kong tinatagi ang mag pahayag ni… Gracioso Jr. sa kanyang sinumpaang salaysay at mga panayaman sa media na inuugnay ako sa mga pangyayaring hindi ko ginawa,” she said.

articles.title: Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could ‘take out’ Los Angeles, San Diego
articles.summary: California officials, including Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, criticize Trump's remarks as dangerous and potentially compromising to public safety

blocks.text: WARNING. US President Donald Trump speaks to the media before boarding Air Force One for departure to Miami, Florida, at Palm Beach International Airport in West Palm Beach, Florida, US on May 2, 2026. REUTERS/Nathan Howard
California officials, including Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, criticize Trump's remarks as dangerous and potentially compromising to public safety

items: President Trump suggested at a rally that Iran could 'take out' major US cities like Los Angeles and San Diego, prompting backlash from California leaders and some Republicans.
The White House defended Trump's comments, stating they were misinterpreted and emphasizing that America is safer due to his actions against Iran.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

LOS ANGELES, USA – President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could “take out” a major US city like Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing a swift rebuke from California’s Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.

Trump, speaking at a political rally in the state’s farm belt on Monday, October 5, discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and said he was determined to “see a tremendous victory, because it verifies all the things we did.”

“And again, remember, with the war, it’s just artificial, it’s a little bit high, it’s a small price to pay,” he told the crowd in Grand Island, Nebraska, apparently referring to rising prices of fuel, fertilizer and other products attributed to energy market disruptions from the war.

blocks.caption: Iran urges US voters to vote out Trump’s allies in election

blocks.text: “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let ’em take out Los Angeles, let ’em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it’s going to be over with very soon,” he said.
“It’s essentially almost over with,” Trump went on. “But it’s going to end very soon, and it’s going to end one way or the other.”
On Tuesday, October 6, the White House dismissed criticism of the remark.

“The media freakout over President Trump’s comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn’t been stopped,” White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung said in a social media post. “America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money.”

Trump has shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict before, and he previously downplayed his concerns about the potential for Iran or its allies to launch an attack on US soil.

The comment in rural Nebraska, a state Trump won with more than 55% of the vote in the 2024 presidential election, targeted Democratic-run cities in California, a solidly Democratic state the president often criticizes.
Monday’s comments prompted a backlash from California officials.California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, denounced the Republican president as “deranged and dangerous.”
“After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego,” he wrote on X.

Newsom, who has positioned himself as a major political foil to Trump and is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, juxtaposed a video clip of Trump in Nebraska with mention of the president’s previous rhetoric to justify deploying US military troops to Los Angeles and other cities to fight crime and enforce immigration.

California’s early voting for the November midterm elections started on Monday. The president’s Republican Party has hoped to win more races in the state in recent years, including this year’s gubernatorial election.

Newsom championed the redrawing of California’s congressional map last year to favor Democrats in this year’s election after Trump pushed for conservative-led Texas to redraw its map to boost Republicans.
One of the Republicans running in a competitive race in a redrawn California district near San Diego, Jim Desmond, distanced himself from Trump’s remarks.

“I vehemently disagree with President Trump’s comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander in Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland,” he wrote on X. “No American city is expendable, and no American family should ever be treated as collateral damage.”

US Representative Kevin Kiley, an independent who caucuses with Republicans and is running for re-election in a competitive race in northern California, said in a statement that Trump’s comment was “unhelpful.”
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, a Democrat, said in a statement that Trump’s comment “could potentially compromise our safety.”
Appearing on MS Now on Tuesday, Bass disputed Cheung’s assertion that Trump’s comments were being misinterpreted by a “freaked out” media.

“Well, I’m not sure that he understands that we can hear what the president said,” Bass countered, adding that Cheung’s defense of Trump’s remarks “has no connection to the words that came out of the president’s mouth.”
Los Angeles and San Diego rank as the largest and second-largest cities in California by population.
More than 115,000 active-duty service members are also stationed in San Diego, including Naval Base San Diego, the largest on the US west coast.

“My constituents — including many active duty service members, veterans, and their families — are not acceptable collateral damage in Trump’s stupid war,” US Representative Sara Jacobs, a Democrat, said in a social media post. – Rappler.com

articles.title: David Ellison denies he has ‘politicized’ Skydance despite close Trump links
articles.summary: Ellison admits ‘good relationship’ with administration in remarks to reporters about newly merged media company David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance,…

blocks.text: David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance, denied that he has “politicized” the company despite the close connection he has forged with Donald Trump’s White House over the 20 months of his administration.

“We have a good relationship with this administration,” Ellison acknowledged to reporters at a Tuesday press briefing focused on the now-consummated merger of Paramount Skydance and CNN parent company Warner Bros Discovery.

“I also had a really good relationship with President Biden. I have a good relationship with [Republican South Carolina senator] Tim Scott, and I have a good relationship with Governor Gavin Newsom. I think it is important to talk to everybody on both sides of the aisle … When you’re operating within a business-friendly administration, you should always have those relationships.”
“We want to speak to everybody,” Ellison added. “We do not want to politicize the company.”

Asked about his conversations with Trump about CNN, Ellison did not directly discuss his communications with the president, the network’s most prominent critic. But he said he wanted to clarify that “we have not talked to any political leader of any party about news, other than to say that we want to be in the truth business and we want to be in the trust business. And we believe in complete editorial independence.”

Amid concerns about whether Ellison might move CNN in a more rightward editorial direction, he said that both the cable news network and CBS News would be “completely editorially independent”, echoing a message he delivered earlier in the day during a town hall meeting with company employees.

Ellison also gave an endorsement to the two leaders he has tapped to continue running the two news networks networks he now controls, CNN chief executive Mark Thompson and CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.
On Monday, Thompson told staffers in a memo that he would remain at the merged company, while Skydance also confirmed that Weiss would remain in her role.
“We’re thrilled, obviously, with Mark,” Ellison said. “We’re thrilled with Bari.”

Asked about a potential merging of CBS News and CNN and any cuts – or “synergies” – that might stem from that, Ellison said he and his leadership team would spend the next several months “basically getting under the hood on all of that”. Most of the $6bn in expected savings from the merger would not come from job losses, he said.
Ellison was not asked about Weiss’s performance as the editorial leader of CBS News. When asked specifically about Weiss’s performance by a Guardian reporter in June, Ellison ignored the question.

articles.title: Pornhub returns to Australia after banning access due to age verification rules
articles.summary: Australian adults again able to access the world’s most popular porn site after parent company introduces age checking via Apple devices Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast…

blocks.text: Australian adults will be able to access Pornhub once again after the site brought in age-checking on Apple devices in response to legal requirements that initially saw the site block users.

In March, Aylo, the parent company of the most popular porn site on the internet, blocked Australian users after online safety codes required adult websites verify users as being 18 or older or face potential fines of $49.5m.
Aylo said at the time the age checking requirements would not protect minors and create data privacy risks for users required to provide their personal information to the sites verifying ages.
Shortly after access was blocked, three virtual private network apps that allow users to appear to be outside Australia rocketed up the app download charts.
On Wednesday, Aylo’s vice-president for brand and community, Alex Kekesi, said Pornhub would return to Australia now that Apple had implemented age-checking features at the device level in iOS.
Apple rolled out its new age checks in Australia last month after a UK rollout earlier this year.

Under the requirements, people can confirm their age with Apple by using a credit card, scanning their passport, driver’s licence or government ID. But for existing Apple account holders, the company can check the existing credit card on file, or by looking at the length of time that person has held that account.
Content filtering and restrictions from downloading apps identified at 18 or older are in place until a user is identified as being over 18.

Kekesi said Apple’s approach “set a benchmark by enabling child safety features automatically for users who have not verified that they are adults, ultimately, making every phone or tablet kid-safe as a starting point”.
Aylo would restore access to Pornhub users in Australia who have confirmed their age through Apple’s age-verification process, Kekesi said.

“In our view, Apple’s Australian device-level age-verification update offers one of the strongest and hardest-to-circumvent protections currently available for helping prevent minors from accessing age-inappropriate content,” Kekesi said.
“We congratulate Apple on their extended age requirements for Apple accounts in Australia.”
Kekesi urged Apple to roll out the feature globally and for Microsoft and Google to follow suit.
“We are determined to be part of this solution and want to collaborate with government, civil society and tech partners to arrive at an effective kid-safe-by-default solution.”
after newsletter promotion
When Aylo blocked Australian users in March, the office of the eSafety commissioner said it was ultimately a business decision for them.

The sex worker advocacy group Scarlet Alliance warned the requirement risked having a “chilling effect” on platforms willing to host online advertising for their services and content, and could lead to over-filtering of content, including sexual health information, due to concern about being in breach.
The rollout of the age-check on Pornhub in the UK has not been smooth. The media regualtor, Ofcom, is investigating whether minors could still access the site.
“We are concerned that Aylo may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing before implementing its new age assurance process,” Ofcom said last month.
“As a result, we are concerned that Aylo’s process may not be highly effective at preventing children from seeing pornography.”
Aylo said it would cooperate fully with the investigation, and Apple’s age-check method was one of the strongest and hardest to circumvent models available.

The boom in popularity of VPN apps following the code introduction in March appears to have been short-lived. The VPN apps that had rapidly entered the Top 25 downloads chart, according to Sensor Tower in March, have since slipped back out of the rankings.

articles.title: Hunter Valley community group wins landmark high court climate change case
articles.summary: Ruling on Mount Pleasant coalmine shows ‘we cannot continue to dig up coal … and pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us’, group says A Hunter Valley community group has won Australia’s…

blocks.text: A Hunter Valley community group has won Australia’s first high court case to consider climate change, in a ruling advocates say sets a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales.

In a landmark judgment, the nation’s highest court upheld a unanimous ruling by the NSW court of appeal that overturned MACH Energy’s proposed expansion of its Mount Pleasant coalmine in Musswellbrook.

In a 3-2 split ruling, the high court dismissed the coal company’s appeal, with a majority of judges finding the state’s planning commission was required and failed to consider how to mitigate the greenhouse gas emissions that would be generated by the mine when the coal is sold and burnt overseas.

A majority of the court found the Independent Planning Commission failed to consider imposing conditions aimed at minimising these emissions – known as Scope 3 emissions – to the greatest extent possible.
The Mount Pleasant expansion would double the mine’s coal output to 21m tonnes per annum until 2048 and 98% of the projected emissions are scope 3 emissions.
Wendy Wales is a retired science teacher and the president of the Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group (DAMSHEG) — the community group that brought the original case.

“Today the high court has said what we have always known: we cannot dig up coal, ship it overseas, watch it drive climate change, and then pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us and won’t be felt by us,” she said.
“The droughts, the bushfires, the floods — are directly connected to greenhouse gases, and massive fossil fuel projects like Mt Pleasant Optimisation simply “add fuel to the fire”.
“We can’t ignore physics, chemistry and biology. We must live within nature’s limits and this ruling endorses that.”

Wales said the ruling was acknowledgement that many Australians had “already suffered extreme weather devastation”. She said lawmakers needed to turn their “full attention” to addressing climate change.
“Now the true and complete long term costs of export coal on Australians, via the climate impact from burning that coal, must be considered,” she said.
The proceedings, brought by MACH Energy, were the first time Australia’s highest court had been asked to consider a case on climate grounds.
MACH had appealed a 2025 decision by the NSW court of appeal that overturned a massive expansion of the company’s Mount Pleasant mine in Muswellbrook.

The court of appeal found in favour of the Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group, ruling the NSW Independent Planning Commission was required and failed to consider the impacts of all emissions associated with the project on the local environment.

In the initial proceedings brought by the community group in the Land and Environment Court, that court ruled in favour of MACH Energy. Wales, her partner Tony Longeran and the DAMSHEG community group have pursued the case through the courts for more than four years.
Comment has been sought from MACH Energy.
More details to follow

articles.title: Palace rejects VP Sara's claim that Marcos admin was behind cash delivery claims
articles.summary: “Wala nang masisira kay VP Sara; nasa katawan na niya ‘yan."

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and Vice President Sara Duterte on January 25, 2024.
STAR / KJ Rosales

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang dismissed Vice President Sara Duterte’s claims that the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was behind the multi-million-peso cash delivery allegations against her to undermine her reputation.
“Wala nang masisira kay VP Sara; nasa katawan na niya ‘yan,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in an interview on Tuesday, October 6, when asked to react to Duterte’s allegations.
(There’s nothing left to tarnish about Vice President Sara; it’s already on her.)

Earlier Tuesday, Duterte accused the Marcos administration and its communications officials of orchestrating efforts to damage her reputation and redirecting the president’s corruption issues toward her.
This came after dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. claimed that more than P2 billion in cash was delivered to her upon the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Duterte denied the allegations anew and reiterated that she did not personally know Gracioso.
Pointing fingers
Castro said the vice president is just pointing fingers at others because she can no longer present valid evidence to debunk the allegations.
“Siguro ‘yun talaga ‘yung mangyayari kapag ka wala nang mahanap na pang-defense, magtuturo ka na lang ng iba. Wala pang naibibigay na ebidensiya na wala silang natanggap,” Castro said.
(Perhaps that’s what happens when you can’t find anything to defend yourself, you’ll point to others. No evidence has been presented to prove that they received nothing.)

The Palace spokesperson also answered Duterte’s claims that Gracioso’s statements are intended to support the alleged unexplained wealth allegations against her in the ongoing impeachment trial, saying that the vice president has failed to properly deny the allegations against her.
“So ang pangulo, lagi niyang itinuturo. Hindi kayang ibenta ng pangulo ang bansa sa dayuhan. Isa itong karumal-dumal na gawain, so ‘wag natin itong tularan,” Castro said.
(She’s always pointing to the president. The president cannot sell the country to foreigners. It’s a heinous act, so let’s not follow this.)

articles.title: Jaguar targets young Americans with Type 01 EV – but it’s too long for UK parking spaces
articles.summary: Latest model is launching in New York to target rich US buyers – and is more than 5.2 metres long and 2 metres wide It has no rear window, will not fit into a UK parking space and – starting at…

blocks.text: It has no rear window, will not fit into a UK parking space and – starting at £130,000 – ($172,000) is aimed squarely at rich tech industry buyers driving the wide open roads of America.
Jaguar’s electric car, the Type 01, was launched in New York on Tuesday night and marks the culmination of a two-year rebrand that has been one of the most scrutinised in automotive history.

Bosses hope the vehicle will appeal to a younger, richer audience than the manufacturer’s previous “shrinking and ageing” customer base of “men in their 50s”, said Rawdon Glover, 58, Jaguar’s managing director.
With an ultra-long bonnet, low roof and muscular design, the Type 01 is a sharp departure from its predecessor, the F-Type. It is also double the F-Type’s starting price of about £62,000.

blocks.caption: The Jaguar Type 01 is intended to appeal to buyers beyond the carmaker’s usual base. Photograph: PR

blocks.text: Buyers are likely to be rich, “urban” and “very design literate, very technology literate”, Glover said. “The person making this purchase will be choosing the car because it’s a bold choice.”
A senior JLR executive close to the Type 01 project put it more bluntly: “It’s the type of car that you park up and everybody stops and says: ‘Fucking hell, what have you just turned up in?’”

blocks.caption: The Type 01 is 2 metres (6ft 5in) wide. Photograph: Mark Fagelson/PR

blocks.text: The launch comes at a critical juncture for parent company Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), which has grappled with falling sales as cheaper Chinese rivals eat into its UK market share. It is still recovering from a massive cyber-attack last year that cost the economy an estimated £1.9bn.

JLR recently announced 4,000 job cuts in an attempt to save £1.7bn over two years, citing “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”. The Guardian understands Jaguar employees working on the Type 01 programme were offered voluntary redundancy along with the rest of JLR’s non-manufacturing workforce.

blocks.caption: The Type 01 front cabin.  Photograph: Jaguar Land Rover PR

blocks.text: The car will go on sale in early 2027, with the first deliveries anticipated in the second half of the year.

“It’s really important that we put Jaguar back on a more solid financial footing,” Glover said. Asked if doubling prices would be effective, he said it was better than “to toil away as we have done for the last two decades in the volume premium space”.
Range Rover also unveiled its first fully electric model in September with a starting price of £154,070 compared with £107,530 for its combustion engine predecessor.

Waning demand in China, a key market for luxury cars, has also hit Jaguar hard. Glover revealed that the Type 01 will not launch in the country for “a couple of years. We’ve decided just to hold off on that.”
However, he added that China would eventually be “an important part of the equation … it’s very difficult for any car manufacturer to exclude the single largest car market in the world”.
after newsletter promotion
PB Balaji, the JLR chief executive, has said the parent company will pivot towards North America and target more sales to millionaires and billionaires to turn its fortunes around.

Glover admitted that while the Type 01’s launch was in New York, it “absolutely” could have been in Silicon Valley instead, reflecting the type of buyer Jaguar is targeting. He recently took a prototype to the offices of Nvidia, the California-based AI company, whose boss, Jensen Huang, had a ride and “loved it”.

The car has no rear window, instead mounting a rear-facing camera where a traditional mirror would be. The car produces more than 1,000 horsepower and Jaguar says it will travel up to 400 miles on a single charge.

It follows a controversial rebrand that started with an ad in late 2024 featuring stern-faced models without a car in sight. The ad prompted a backlash online and was followed by the Type 00 concept car that was unveiled in “Miami pink”, which Donald Trump described it as “woke” while Nigel Farage said Jaguar deserved to go bust.
Glover admitted the backlash “wasn’t always easy” but added: “The reality is we will need to attract a new audience.”

It is just as well: at 2 metres (6ft 5in) wide the Type 01 will hog the British country lanes frequented by Jaguar’s old customer base, while at more than 5.2 metres in length it will not fit in a standard 4.8 metre UK parking space.

“There are long cars out there on the market,” Glover argued, adding that a Land Rover Defender with a wheel on the back is longer than the Type 01, which he claimed had the “turning circle of a Fiat 500” with its all-wheel steering. “It is incredibly manoeuvrable.”

The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said: “Jaguar’s new EV is a crucial step in JLR’s plans to invest over £15bn in the UK, and another big vote of confidence in our world-class automotive industry.

“This cutting-edge new model being designed, engineered and built in Britain will support thousands of jobs across the West Midlands and North West, and builds on over £1bn of UK automotive investment secured just last month – marking another step forward in our mission to reindustrialise Britain.”

articles.title: [Vantage Point] Is Del Monte in default? The debt behind the label
articles.summary: The sheer consumer power of the Philippine franchise is precisely why nervous financiers continue to sit at the bargaining table

items: Del Monte Philippines is facing a contractual breach with SEA Diner Holdings, leading to financial uncertainty despite strong consumer demand for its products.
The company's operational profitability is overshadowed by a significant debt burden at the parent company level, which hampers its financial independence and ability to reinvest.
Investors are concerned about the company's future as it struggles with cash flow issues and the looming threat of creditor actions, particularly from SEA Diner, which holds substantial leverage.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Del Monte Philippines remains in an uncured contractual breach with SEA Diner Holdings (S) Pte. Ltd. That doesn’t mean outright bankruptcy, but the mid-2025 default notice put the violation on record, and the temporary truce expired on October 1. The silence since leaves investors in the dark about what, if anything, is holding back an immediate demand for cash.

Enforcement wouldn’t clear grocery shelves overnight. But because SEA Diner’s claim sits directly inside the profitable Philippine unit, any action would siphon off cash meant for operations and reinvestment to satisfy a senior creditor. The immediate threat is not missing pantry staples—it is the quiet loss of financial independence for the company producing them.

Every weekend across Metro Manila, supermarket carts tell a story of unshakable consumer trust. Into wire baskets go red-and-green cans of tomato sauce for family spaghetti, chilled pineapple juice for breakfast, and fruit cocktail for Sunday dessert. To the average grocery shopper, Del Monte represents effortless stability: a heritage staple whose products move off grocery shelves with clockwork regularity.

blocks.caption: HERITAGE. Some of the products of Del Monte Philippines. Courtesy of Del Monte Philippines FB

blocks.text: Few shoppers pushing those carts would ever suspect that behind those cheerful labels sits a company tiptoeing across an agonizingly thin financial wire.

The great paradox of Del Monte is that its core consumer business is genuinely thriving. People are not drinking less juice or cooking less pasta. Factories are humming, checkout lanes are busy, and Del Monte Philippines Inc. (DMPI)—the domestic operating powerhouse—remains remarkably profitable and cash-generative.
The trouble begins the moment that money leaves the factory floor and starts climbing the corporate ladder.

Think of Del Monte’s corporate structure as a sturdy, high-speed locomotive hooked to several overloaded, creaking carriages. Down on the tracks, DMPI is doing all the heavy hauling, generating practically all of the group’s operational earnings.

But up at the parent company, Del Monte Pacific Limited (DMPL), the picture changes completely. DMPL bears a massive wall of debt accumulated over years of aggressive leverage. Most of that load is short-term, meaning lenders expect to be repaid or refinanced right now, not years into the future.

Management argues that seasonal working-capital swings and revolving credit facilities keep the situation in check. But a revolving credit line is only as dependable as the banker holding the keys. When short-term liabilities outstrip liquid resources to this extent, lender goodwill ceases to be an operational cushion—it becomes the structural glue holding the entire house together.

The strain became impossible to hide when Del Monte had to ask regulators for extra time just to publish its annual financial statements. External auditors were not debating whether Filipinos still enjoy pineapple juice.

They held back their signatures because they required documented, interim commitments from lenders before certifying the company could survive another year without tumbling into default. While banks have not pulled the plug, agreeing to hold off on enforcing covenants today is very different from writing a committed, long-term check for tomorrow.

Regulators have since given Del Monte until November 30 to publish its FY2026 annual report and until December 22 to hold its annual meeting. The company’s September 17 disclosure said financing-counterparty discussions had not progressed in the manner or timetable experienced in earlier maturity extensions. It also said third-party valuation work tied to the former US subsidiary remained unfinished, leaving the audit and going-concern review dependent on work still outside management’s complete control.

blocks.caption: [Vantage Point] Del Monte Pacific’s US collapse: Rotten economics inside the can

blocks.text: Among the creditors waiting in the wings, Singapore-based SEA Diner casts the longest shadow. It owns barely a tenth of DMPI, but that slice comes armed with immense leverage: a redeemable preference stake worth over US$156 million, guaranteed dividends that compound aggressively when delayed, and legal veto power over major boardroom decisions.

That is why October 1 has become the date hanging over the entire enterprise. When Del Monte tripped covenants last year, SEA Diner slapped it with a default notice before agreeing to a temporary truce—one that ran strictly until the start of October.

Without a fresh standstill or a restructured deal, the clock finally runs out. SEA Diner gains the immediate legal muscle to demand its capital back with hefty returns, tightening its grip on the very cash engine keeping the entire empire afloat.

That outside date has now passed. As of October 5, Del Monte had announced neither another extension nor a completed restructuring of the preference shares. It had disclosed no Default Exercise Notice, redemption demand or enforcement action. Silence is not proof that SEA Diner has exercised its rights. But investors no longer know what, if anything, restrains those rights after the last publicly disclosed standstill expired.

The market’s reaction underscored the uncertainty. On October 2, the first trading day after the deadline, Del Monte Pacific closed at S$0.060, down 11.76% from the previous close and at its 52-week low.
Volume was more than three times its recent average. The timing does not prove causation, but the selloff shows how much weight investors placed on the unexplained deadline.

Look closer at the cash register, and the math becomes even starker. Even after a strong sales year, nearly all the free cash Del Monte squeezes out of operations is instantly spoken for before it can ever benefit ordinary public shareholders.
It flows immediately out the door to service massive interest bills, pay equipment leases, and appease outside preferred investors who hold first-priority claims on subsidiary earnings.

By the latest quarter, that cash engine was running so hot servicing obligations that it failed to generate enough cash to cover them. Management bridged the shortfall by selling off an old overseas investment—a tactical disposal that buys temporary breathing room, but one that cannot be repeated once the family silver is gone.

None of this means Del Monte products are about to vanish from grocery aisles. The sheer consumer power of the Philippine franchise is precisely why nervous financiers continue to sit at the bargaining table. They know the golden goose is still laying eggs.

The dilemma is who gets to keep them. Market popularity, operating health, and corporate solvency are three entirely different disciplines. A business can run one of the most profitable consumer brands in the country while remaining utterly powerless to prevent banks, bondholders, and preference financiers from intercepting every peso at the door.
For ordinary equity investors, that is the central predicament. Del Monte does not have a consumer product issue; it has a top-heavy capital structure problem.

Until the parent company permanently restructures its mountain of debt, satisfies its auditors, and defuses its ticking preference-capital deadlines, its most beloved household brand will simply be working overtime to service someone else’s balance sheet. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Leandro Leviste faces arrest warrant over alleged Public Service Act violation
articles.summary: A Makati court has issued an arrest warrant against Batangas 1st District Representative Leandro Leviste over an alleged violation of the Public Service Act.

blocks.text: Filtered By: Topstories
News
Published October 7, 2026 7:50am
Batangas 1st District Representative Leandro Leviste. Courtesy: House of Representatives
A Makati court has issued an arrest warrant against Batangas 1st District Representative Leandro Leviste over an alleged violation of the Public Service Act.
Based on the document obtained by GMA News from a high-ranking law enforcement official, the warrant was issued by the Makati Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 235 on October 5.
The warrant was signed by Presiding Judge Ricardo A. Moldez II.
GMA News reached out to Makati RTC but the court has refused to give a statement.
The case involves an alleged violation of Section 25 of Commonwealth Act No. 146, as amended by Republic Act No. 11659 or the Public Service Act.
The court ordered law enforcement officers to arrest Leviste and bring him before the court to be dealt with according to law.
Bail was set at P72,000.

A copy was furnished to the Philippine National Police Directorate for Investigation and Detective Management (DIDM) in Camp Crame and the concerned chief of police or station commander. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Chinese state firms remitted P319 million to Sara Duterte-linked company — Hontiveros
articles.summary: The Anti-Money Laundering Council had previously flagged these transactions as covered and suspicious transaction reports due to a lack of legitimate underlying transactions.

blocks.text: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte gestures as she leaves the Hall of Justice in Quezon City, Metro Manila on Sept. 11, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — Chinese state-owned enterprises with direct ties to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Beijing’s foreign influence apparatus have remitted millions of pesos to Cale88 Foods Corp., a company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte.
During the impeachment trial on October 6, Sen. Risa Hontiveros revealed that her office’s research uncovered deep geopolitical links behind the P319 million that entered Calle88 from China.
The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) had previously flagged these transactions as covered and suspicious transaction reports due to a lack of legitimate underlying transactions.
According to Hontiveros, one of the entities that sent money to Calle88 is China National Township Enterprises.

“Base po sa research ng opisina ko, dating directly under the Ministry of Agriculture sa China at naging isang large state-owned agricultural enterprise under the supervision of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council,” Hontiveros said.

(Based on my office’s research, it was previously directly under the Ministry of Agriculture in China and became a large state-owned agricultural enterprise under the supervision of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council.)
She added that the public profiles of China National Township Enterprises openly mention being "committed to serving the implementation of the country's Belt and Road Initiative and foreign policy.”

Another enterprise is Beijing Jianweifang Food Co., owned by the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group, which acts as its Series A investor and has maintained a strategic cooperation agreement with the Beijing firm since 2019.
She said that the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group is "not an ordinary company" but a Chinese state-owned enterprise that actively advances the interests of the CCP.

“It's a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party. Sa mismong corporate governance structure ng Xinjiang Fruit may institutional Chinese Communist Party organization na naka-embed,” Hontiveros said.

(It is a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party. Embedded within the very corporate governance structure of Xinjiang Fruit is an institutional Chinese Communist Party organization.)

When asked by Hontiveros whether the AMLC is actively investigating these Chinese companies and their geopolitical linkages, AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura said that he was unable to answer.
“The only documents related to what we were subpoenaed po 'yung pong mga na-submit po namin na…Summary report po, financial investigation report, financial investigation report,” Buenaventura said.
(The only documents related to what we were subpoenaed for are the ones we submitted, which are the summary report and the financial investigation reports.)
In a statement on October 5, the Chinese Embassy denied that Beijing had ties to a "Philippine political faction."
Calle88 was listed among the business interests connected with Sara Duterte in her 2022–2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.
However, records from the Securities and Exchange Commission show that Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, was an incorporator, director and shareholder of Calle88 from 2021 to 2024.
His ownership reportedly reached 47.5% in 2024, but his name no longer appeared as a shareholder in 2025.

articles.title: Christa Pike awake after failed Tennessee execution: lawyers
articles.summary: A death row inmate who survived a botched execution last week is conscious and talking in hospital, according to her lawyers, who want to commute her death sentence to life imprisonment without…

image.caption: Christa Pike was transported from prison to hospital after last week's botched executionImage: George Walker IV/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A prisoner who survived an attempt to carry out the death penalty in Tennessee, the United States, last week is conscious and speaking as she continues to receive treatment in hospital.
"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," the inmate's attorneys said in a statement on Tuesday.
"Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented."

Pike, who was sentenced to death for the beating, stabbing and murder of a classmate in 1995, survived two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital – which her lawyers said left her arms burned and blistered.
Christa Pike not 'free of further serious risk'
"She's still in the ICU," said Dr. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery in Atlanta in neighboring Georgia, who consulted as an expert for Pike's legal team.

"She has recovered to a certain degree that she's able to be off a ventilator and able to speak, but in no way would I announce her free of further serious risk. There's still a lot of bad things that can happen here, even when everyone is doing their job well."
Tuesday's updates were the first indication that Pike's condition has improved since the failed execution attempt at a Nashville prison last Wednesday.

Her attorneys thanked first responders and medical staff who they said have "treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her" – as they prepare to go to court on Wednesday seeking to learn more about what went wrong with the lethal injection.

blocks.caption: Christa Pike was sentenced to death on March 30, 1996 for her role as a teenager in the torture-murder of her 19-year-old schoolmateImage: WBIR-TV/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pike's attorneys seeking to commute sentence
The lawyers are seeking a court order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence, including drug lot numbers, records and other information from the attempted execution.
Ultimately, they are looking to have Pike's sentence commuted to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
While Dr. Zivot said Pike's current state "bodes well for a good recovery," her attorneys warned that her prognosis is still "unclear" and said she faces "a long recovery."
"Christa is a survivor and will take recovery one day at a time," they said.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, which publishes data and analysis on capital punishment in the United States, Pike is the first prisoner ever to survive "after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs."

articles.title: FAA investigating after Delta plane 'clipped' Air Canada aircraft at LAX
articles.summary: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it is investigating after a Delta Air Lines plane "clipped" an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday.

image.caption: People take pictures of a plane landing at Los Angeles International Airport in July. (Daniel Cole/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it is investigating after a Delta Air Lines plane "clipped" an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday.
Incident occurred as Delta plane was taxiing and Air Canada plane was being towed
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says it is investigating after a Delta Air Lines plane "clipped" an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday.
The aviation agency says the incident occurred around 10:30 a.m. local time as the Delta plane was taxiing for departure, and the Air Canada plane was being towed toward the gate.
An Air Canada spokesperson says there are no reported injuries.
Sean Davidson says in a statement that Air Canada Flight 785 had arrived from Toronto before "an aircraft operated by another airline made contact with its tail."
He says the plane will be taken out of service for inspection and repairs.
The U.S. agency says the Delta plane's left wingtip clipped the Air Canada aircraft's horizontal stabilizer, a wing-likestructure at the tail of a plane.

articles.title: LIST: Duterte-Carpio bank accounts, balances detailed in impeachment trial
articles.summary: Here is a summary of the banks testifying on the Duterte-Carpio money trail as prosecutors try to determine whether year-end account balances line up with what was declared in the Vice President's…

blocks.text: FINANCIAL RECORDS. The Senate impeachment court receives tax and bank records of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 30, 2026.
Senate Public Relations and Information Bureau

Here is a summary of the banks testifying on the Duterte-Carpio money trail as prosecutors try to determine whether year-end account balances line up with what was declared in the Vice President's SALNs

items: Prosecutors in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial are examining bank accounts to verify the accuracy of her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs), which allegedly do not reflect substantial bank balances.

The prosecution has identified at least 30 active accounts across eight banks, with combined year-end balances exceeding P59 million in 2022, P71 million in 2023, and varying amounts in subsequent years.

Bank representatives are being called to authenticate account records, with initial testimonies revealing discrepancies between reported balances and Duterte's SALNs, while further bank presentations are expected in upcoming trial days.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – After examining billions of pesos in reported transactions through the Anti-Money Laundering Council, prosecutors in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial are now going to what could be the most consequential part: the banks that actually held the accounts.

More representatives from several banks are expected to authenticate the underlying accounts and records of Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, as prosecutors seek to establish whether the couple’s bank balances were properly reflected in the Vice President’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs).
Private prosecutor James Bryan Ibrahim Alih said the records cover at least 30 active accounts across eight banks for the years 2022 to 2025.
According to the prosecution’s offer of testimony, the accounts had combined year-end balances of more than P59 million in 2022, P71 million in 2023, P22 million in 2024, and P35 million in 2025.

blocks.caption: UNDECLARED? Screenshot from prosecution’s offer of testimony on Tuesday, October 6, 2026.

blocks.text: Yet recall that in each of those years, Duterte’s SALNs did not separately list any cash on hand or cash in bank.

The prosecution alleges that the balances do not match Duterte’s SALNs. Her lawyers have previously argued that cash and bank deposits were included under the broader “other personal properties” category. The testimonies of bank officials are expected to provide the more precise year-end balances needed to make that comparison.
Here are the banks and officers identified so far:

Eunice Sumatra, manager of LandBank’s San Pedro-Davao City branch, became the first bank witness on Tuesday, October 6. Prosecutors called her to authenticate records involving one payroll bank account with account number ending 8998 in the name of Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

Raquel Dela Cerna, manager of LandBank’s Davao R. Magsaysay branch, followed Sumatra and authenticated an active account belonging to Carpio ending in 2730. She disclosed year-end balances of P505,517.35 in 2022, P953,681.42 in 2023, P115,824.20 in 2024, and P1,358,373.07 in 2025.

blocks.caption: LANDBANK. Screenshot during the direct examination of Cerna on October 6.

blocks.text: Cerna also mentioned that the branch had two accounts linked to the Vice President, which were now closed.
During cross-examination, Cerna agreed that marriage alone does not make one spouse a joint account holder or authorized signatory of an account held by the other.
AUB is among the banks the prosecution is expected to present. As of October 6, no representative from the bank had yet taken the stand.
PSBank is among the banks the prosecution is expected to present. As of October 6, no representative from the bank had yet taken the stand.

AMLC earlier presented an August 1, 2024 suspicious transaction report involving Carpio’s PSBank accounts that cited “drug trafficking and related offenses.” The STR narrative referred to a criminal complaint over the alleged 2017 importation of P6.4 billion worth of shabu and noted that Carpio had active peso and dollar accounts with the bank.
Metrobank is among the banks the prosecution is expected to present. As of October 6, no representative from the bank had yet taken the stand.
BPI is among the banks the prosecution is expected to present. As of October 6, no representative from the bank had yet taken the stand.

BPI is already a significant part of the impeachment record because it asked AMLC to correct 13 covered transaction reports involving Carpio after discovering erroneous amounts caused by what the bank described as a system bug.
AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura confirmed Tuesday that AMLC validated BPI’s corrections.
PNB is among the banks the prosecution is expected to present. As of October 6, no representative from the bank had yet taken the stand.

PNB records could be notable because AMLC testimony on October 5 identified P18 million in withdrawals from a Carpio account at PNB on August 6, 2024, part of P41 million he withdrew from PNB and BDO that day.
BDO is among the banks the prosecution is expected to present. As of October 6, no representative from the bank had yet taken the stand.

BDO records could likewise draw scrutiny after AMLC testimony identified P23 million in withdrawals from Carpio’s account at BDO on August 6, 2024, forming part of the same P41-million single-day withdrawal total.
The prosecution is expected to complete the bank-by-bank presentation over the succeeding trial days. – Rappler.com
