articles.title: Want to buy GCash shares? How retail investors can join the IPO
articles.summary: Here’s what you need to know about the offer period and what to consider before deciding whether to buy

blocks.text: Here’s what you need to know about the offer period and what to consider before deciding whether to buy

items: Filipinos can invest in GCash through GStocks PH in the GCash app.
Secondary shares sold by existing shareholders make up 80% of GCash's initial public offering.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Filipinos can now buy into GCash before it officially makes its Philippine Stock Exchange debut, with the public offer period starting Tuesday, October 6.

One of the easiest routes is through GStocks PH inside the GCash app itself. Investors can open Invest, select GStocks PH, then tap the IPO banner. GStocks PH requires an eligible account with enough money in its trading wallet. Opening an account generally requires users to be at least 18 years old, have a Philippine SIM, a fully verified GCash account, and a valid government ID.
The minimum GCash IPO order through GStocks PH is 100 shares, worth P660 at the P6.60 offer price.

Retail investors can also participate as local small investors through PSE EASy. The PSE said all LSI subscriptions for the Mynt IPO must be submitted through the platform, which requires investors to nominate a PSE trading participant or broker. The usual LSI ceiling is P100,000. Investors with existing brokerage accounts may also check whether their broker is accepting IPO orders.
The offer period runs until noon on Monday, October 12, giving retail investors until then to submit their subscriptions and complete any required payment and documentation.
Regular trading under the ticker GCASH is scheduled to begin on October 20, when allocated IPO shares can start trading on the PSE.

blocks.caption: For GCash’s early private equity backers, record IPO will be ultimate payday

blocks.text: In an investor briefing on Tuesday, GCash’s top executives made their case for why the homegrown e-wallet is a good buy.

Mynt had 41.5 million monthly active users by June, about four times the active users of its nearest competitor. Its adjusted revenue grew at a 54% compound annual growth rate from 2023 to 2025, while net income rose at a 64.4% CAGR over the same period, reaching P17.25 billion in 2025.

In other words, both revenue and profit were growing quite strongly over that two-year stretch. Net income reached another P10.82 billion in the first half of 2026. Management is eyeing lending, merchant services, overseas users, and deeper use of the app as the next avenue of growth.

But investors also have reasons to look closely at the deal. Around 80% of the IPO consists of secondary shares being sold by existing shareholders, meaning most of the money raised from those shares goes to the sellers rather than Mynt as fresh capital. Management has stressed that this does not represent a full exit by its strategic shareholders, but it does show that several early private equity investors see this as a good time to cash out. (READ: Meet the new cornerstone investors lining up for GCash’s record IPO)

Remember too the oft-repeated investing maxim that a good company can still be a bad investment at the wrong price. GCash is also coming to market at a hefty valuation. At P6.60, its roughly P442-billion valuation works out to about 24.6x its latest trailing 12-month earnings through June, against the PSEi’s 9.87x multiple as of October 2. – Rappler.com

blocks.caption: PSE enters new territory with GCash’s IPO. But to thrive, it must go further.

articles.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
articles.summary: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.

image.caption: Munich hosted the 1972 Summer Olympic GamesImage: Sven Hoppe/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Munich's bid for the 2036 Summer Olympics will be up against at least six candidates from Europe, Asia, and Africa. On Tuesday, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced that, in addition to Germany, Hungary, Turkey, India, Qatar, South Korea, and South Africa all intend to bid for the Games. All are currently engaged in the "Continuous Dialogue" stage of the bidding process with the IOC.

However, there could be further applicants, as the deadline for interested parties to submit a bid is October 31. The candidates are to present their plans virtually to the Future Host Commission in November. In March 2027, the IOC is to deliberate, analyze, and narrow down the field of applicants to a group selected to enter into the Strategic Dialogue stage.
A subsequent Targeted Dialogue stage with one or more bidders is planned for 2028, with the final decision on the 2036 Olympic host expected at the IOC Session in the summer of 2029.
However, the IOC did not disclose exactly which cities, alongside Munich, are in the running – although Ahmedabad, Doha, Budapest, and Istanbul are seen as possible hopefuls.

Munich secured its bid late last month after beating the Cologne/Rhine-Ruhr region in a vote by delegates of the German Olympic Sports Confederation. The city last hosted the Games in 1972. Berlin had withdrawn its bid in the days leading up to the vote.

blocks.caption: As a swimmer Kirsty Coventry won two Olympic gold medals for ZimbabweImage: Patrick Meinhardt/AFP

blocks.text: 'Best possible experience for the athletes'
"Wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do," IOC President Kirsty Coventry said.

"As an athlete, you spend years working to make your Olympic dream come true. The experience you have when you finally reach the Olympic Games stays with you for the rest of your life," added the former swimmer who won gold in the 200-meter backstroke for Zimbabwe at the 2004 Athens and 2008 Beijing Summer Games.
"That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point."
Munich bid sees itself as well-positioned

The IOC is to evaluate the bidders' proposals based on "technical factors." These include a master plan for competition venues and the athlete experience, the financing strategy, political and public support, the capacity to deliver the event, and a sustainability strategy. The German Olympic Sports Confederation believes Munich is well-positioned in all these areas.

The Munich bid is not focused solely on 2036 but was also designed with 2040 and 2044 in mind. If it misses out on 2036, Munich can expect to face a similarly large pool of competitors for the following two Summer Games. According to an IOC statement, there are National Olympic Committees "taking part in noncommittal talks with the IOC about hosting future Olympic Games beyond 2036."
This article was adapted from German.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 34: Discrepancies in SALN, bank transactions
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said on the 34th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that the total net worth of Duterte and her husband, Manases…

blocks.text: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said on the 34th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that the total net worth of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as stated in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) from 2007 to 2025 does not match the amount of their bank transactions.
Escudero made the observation based on the testimony of Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura.

“P424 million ang pumasok at lumabas sa bank accounts ni Vice President Duterte at ng kanyang asawa from 2022 to 2025. I try to bring things to their absurd possibility to find out and test the hypothesis. In-add ko iyong SALN ng Pangalawang Pangulo mula 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025. Hindi naman dapat i-add ‘yun kasi iba’t ibang taon. [Pero] in total, P336 million. Hindi pa rin umabot ng P424 million. Meaning to say, on the assumption na walang ginastos mula sa lahat na assets nila at lahat na dineposit sa bangko, hindi pa rin aabot sa ganitong kalaking halaga,” he said.

“The P4.4 billion covering the period 2007 to 2025, we tried to add all of the amounts in the combined SALNs for the covered period of 2007 to 2025. It totaled only P840 million. You would need five times at least five times the combined SALN total from 2007 to 2025 to be able to explain the huge amount of P4.4 billion in transactions,” he added.

Before Escudero made the observation, the AMLC official said that Cale88 Foods Corporation, one of the business interests of Carpio, recorded over P1.2 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions from 2022 to 2025.
The AMLC official also said that the P1.2 billion figure includes the P319 million remittances to Cale88 from China.

Buenaventura also said there were no rectifications made to the records they already submitted to the Senate impeachment court because BPI’s request for correction back in April, reducing the covered and suspicious bank transactions under Carpio’s name from P2 billion to P2 million, was not taken by the AMLC as gospel truth.

“It was not rectified because there was nothing at the time that we submitted our records, submitted before the House. When we were subpoenaed, these were the records standing in our database. Now, there was a request. We validated that,” Buenaventura said.
Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III was also not convinced that the glitch reported by the BPI, which prompted the request for correction to the AMLC, indeed happened.

“Ang tagal-tagal na panahon na meron akong account sa bangko. Ni minsan, hindi ako nakaranas nun, o may kakilala man lang na naging bilyon [ang pera] dahil sa bank system glitch. Nangyayari ba talaga ito na P2 billion naging P2 million?” Sotto said.
Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros said Chinese firms “advancing the interests of the Chinese Communist Party” were behind the P319 million inward remittances to Cale88.
She said these include China National Township Enterprises and Beijing Zhenweifang Food Company, supposedly owned by the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group, as stated in the company’s own materials.
Senator Robin Padilla, meanwhile, denied receiving money from China even as he admitted that he is affiliated with Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines.

It was former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV who said that Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines, which named the Vice President as one of its incorporators, received P150 million from China.

"Sana po masabi lang doon sa ating mga kasama na, tutal hindi naman nabanggit dito 'yung sa Tapang at Malasakit, hinihingi ko po na 'wag naman kaming madamay lahat. Kasi kasama kami diyan eh. Hindi naman po 'yan nabanggit dito sa korte. Binanggit 'yan ni former senator Trillanes na hindi sa korteng ito," Padilla said.

(I hope the parties realize that since the Tapang at Malasakit was not initially mentioned here in the trial, I ask that we not all be implicated. Because we are part of that alliance. It wasn't brought up here in the trial. It was former senator Trillanes who mentioned it, but not in this court.)

Senator-Judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson also said that the legislative intent of the provision on the prohibitions against political harassment under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) is solely meant for the election period.

“I was here in 2001 when we passed [Republic Act] 9160. This amendment was introduced by the late senator Nene Pimentel, because at that time, we were in the opposition. So ang intent nito, doon lang sa election period na hindi mako-cover ng batas lahat ng kandidato,” he said.
(The intent of this was only for the election period when the law cannot cover all candidates.
Before the day ended, Escudero ruled that the bank records of the Vice President and her husband, as submitted by the banks to the court, enjoy a presumption of regularity.

Escudero made the ruling since the defense team of the Vice President refused to stipulate, or agree, that the bank records are authentic, prompting the prosecution to present the bank officials to confirm the authenticity as well as the balance of the accounts under the names of the Vice President and her husband.

“To the extent that any record independently qualifies as an official record and is entitled to a presumption of regularity, that presumption is rebuttable and does not establish the truth or accuracy of every entry,” he said.

Escudero said that this is in accordance with Rule 4, Section 1 of the Rules on Evidence, which regards an electronic document as equivalent to an original under the original document rule when it is a printout of other or other output readable by sight or other means and shown to reflect the data accurately.
Side comments

Ahead of Escudero's remark, defense counsel Mark Vinluan apologized to the senator-judges over his cross-examination that dwelled on the punitive provisions of the AMLA for those who will violate the confidentiality clause. The Senate court ruled that impeachment proceedings are not covered by such confidentiality.

"We just want to test the credibility of the witness. It is never our intention to cause intimidation to the members of the Honorable impeachment court. I personally apologize and I can commit to be more circumspect moving forward," Vinluan added.
House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro Party-list said that the direct examination of Buenaventura took six hours on Monday due to numerous objections by the defense.

Ridon was responding to defense counsel Sheila Sison’s manifestation before the Senate impeachment court that they should not be rushed in conducting their cross-examination on Monday, October 5. —GMA News

articles.title: Germany shaken by espionage and treason allegations
articles.summary: The former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, has been accused of spying for a foreign country. Never before has a German official of August Hanning's stature been accused of…

image.caption: Former BND chief August Hanning has been arrested on espionage chargesImage: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: If the allegations are confirmed, it would be an espionage case of historic proportions for Germany: August Hanning, former head of the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), has been arrested, with the federal prosecutor accusing him of espionage, treason and attempted treason.

August Hanning, now 80, headed the BND from 1998 to 2005. But even before then, he had enjoyed a meteoric rise within the security apparatus. After leaving the BND, he served as state secretary in the Federal Interior Ministry, then moved into the private sector and worked as a security consultant.

According to the federal prosecutor's office, his informant was his former chief-of-staff, named in the statement only as Manfred D.*, who went on to hold this position under Hanning's successors from March 2012 to March 2026. D. thus had access to a great deal of classified information.
Former German spy chief arrested for espionage
Classified information from the chancellor's office

Manfred D. is alleged to have passed on nearly 2,000 BND documents — some of them highly sensitive — to Hanning over the course of several years in exchange for money. Hanning is then said to have used the information in his private consultancy business.

The most serious allegation is that Hanning is said to have maintained close contact with an employee of a foreign intelligence service for years and to have leaked classified information to him. It is not known which country was involved, but reports say it is not Russia.

Investigators also mention an analysis that Hanning is said to have prepared for an employee of another foreign intelligence service. However, it is not certain whether the analysis ever reached that person.

The classified information also concerned the routine meetings of the heads of German security agencies at the chancellery. Topics included, among other things, the Iranian nuclear program and analyses of the Russian armed forces.

Since intelligence from foreign partner agencies is also said to have been shared in this context, this could also undermine their trust in the German BND and lead to difficulties in future intelligence cooperation with Germany.
Hanning came under scrutiny in an entirely different context
"A good agent is one who doesn't draw attention to himself," Hanning was once quoted as saying. When he finally drew attention to himself, it was in an entirely different context.

In September 2025, the Hamburg state police searched Hanning's home and offices in connection with the famous case of the kidnapping involving Christina Block, heiress to the steakhouse restaurant chain Block House. State prosecutors in Hamburg accused her of having ordered the kidnapping of her two youngest children in late 2023 due to a custody dispute.

A little over a year before the operation to bring the children back, there is said to have already been a failed kidnapping attempt. At the time, there were suspicions that Hanning was involved, which he denies.

But during a search in 2025, investigators found an electronic storage device containing top-secret BND documents. The police handed the documents over to the federal prosecutor's office, which launched a covert investigation against Hanning and Manfred D. in May 2026. The most recent documents found so far are said to date from June 2022.
Greens demand consequences

Throughout its history, the BND has seen a number of espionage cases, some of them spectacular. In the 1960s, Heinz Felfe headed the "Counterintelligence: Soviet Union" division while simultaneously working for the Soviet secret service, the KGB.

In 2014, a BND employee was exposed as a spy for the US CIA. There is also an ongoing trial against a BND agent accused of betraying secrets to Russia's FSB in September and October 2022 — that is, after the start of the war in Ukraine. Yet never before has a former official of August Hanning's stature been at the center of suspicion of espionage.

"The BND launched extensive internal investigations early on and without delay, which corroborated the suspicions," said current BND President Martin Jäger. "For the BND and for me, there can be no compromises when it comes to internal security."

However, there was some fierce criticism from the political sphere. Günter Krings of the conservative governing party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), told the Rheinische Post newspaper: "The mere suspicion that a former BND chief is selling secrets is damaging to trust in our security agencies."

Konstantin von Notz of the environmentalist Green Party and deputy chair of the parliamentary committee that oversees the intelligence services said: "These are serious and grave allegations that have been leveled against August Hanning." Speaking on behalf of his party, he called for greater scrutiny of lobbying activities by former top officials and those with the highest security clearances. "These are clearly also a gateway for hostile intelligence services," von Notz said. The federal government must put an immediate stop to these "illegitimate practices."

Clara Bünger, domestic policy spokesperson for the socialist Left Party group in the Bundestag, went even further: "The investigations against former BND chief Hanning show once again: The intelligence services themselves are a security risk."
This article was originally written in German.

*Editor's note: DW follows the German press code, which stresses the importance of protecting the privacy of suspected criminals or victims and urges us to refrain from revealing full names in such cases.

articles.title: AfD candidate elected speaker of German regional parliament for first time
articles.summary: Although Tobias Rausch's role is largely symbolic, opponents have described the result as a watershed moment.

blocks.text: A month after Germany's far-right AfD scored a decisive victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, the party's candidate Tobias Rausch has been elected as parliament speaker there too.
Not since World War Two has a far-right party secured the post of speaker, and protesters outside the building in Magdeburg held up banners saying, "Never again is now".
Although the AfD fell three seats short of a majority in last month's election, Rausch, 35, comfortably won Tuesday's vote with the support of 9 MPs from other parties.
"The days of political firewalls should be a thing of the past," Rausch said after the vote, rejecting a post-war consensus in German politics not to work with the far right.

This was the first time since last month's state vote that Saxony-Anhalt's newly elected representatives had gathered in parliament, and regional Greens party leader Susan Sziborra-Seidlitz said "a line has been crossed" with the election of a far-right speaker of parliament, and it was a watershed moment.
"We will not let ourselves be intimidated, and we will not sit by when rights are curtailed either here or for people in the state," she said.
The AfD is considered pro-Russian and anti-immigrant, with plans to segregate child refugees in schools, as well as intolerant towards the LGBT community.

Within Saxony-Anhalt it is also classed as "right-wing extremist" by domestic intelligence, a description rejected by party leaders. Until now its members have sat on the right fringe of the state parliament, but ahead of Tuesday's inaugural session it successfully argued that it should now sit in the centre.

articles.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
articles.summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival…

image.caption: 'That's all folks,' Warner Bros. and Paramount and their subsidiaries will all be bundled under a new banner: Skydance Corp.Image: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Paramount on Tuesday finalized its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, completing a hostile acquisition that was months in the making and almost faltered at several hurdles.
The takeover cost a total of around $81 billion (roughly €72 billion), or almost $111 billion including the Warner Bros. debts passed on as part of the deal.
The merger brings together two of the oldest US filmmaking studios and will form a new giant called Skydance Corporation.
Why Skydance Corp.? Who's behind the new behemoth?
The new name Skydance hails from billionaire investor David Ellison, who first bought out Paramount and its subsidiaries and then moved on to target the much larger fish that is Warner Bros.
The bid faced stiff competition in a bidding war with Netflix, and later scrutiny from US regulators and politicians, but ultimately went through.
"Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry," said Ellison, whose family has ties to US President Donald Trump.
Skydance shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday under the ticker SKYD, while Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders will receive about $31 per share.
The deal closed less than a week after a federal judge in California approved a settlement between Paramount and 12 US states that had sued to block the transaction on antitrust grounds.

As well as the two giant film studios, Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures, the deal also brings together the CBS News and CNN news networks, and the HBO and CBS television brands. Ellison says he plans to merge the subscription streaming platforms Paramount+ and HBO Max.
Ellison will serve as chairman and CEO of the new company. Former Mattel boss Ynon Kreiz is operating as co-CEO in charge of day-to-day operations.

Skydance Corp. looks set to have a total revenue in the region of $70 billion, based on the performance to date of its component parts. It says it's targeting cost savings of around $6 billion within three years as it takes advantage of overlaps created by the merger.

articles.title: White House defends Trump comment to let Iran 'take out' LA and San Diego
articles.summary: Gavin Newsom called the remarks "deranged", but the White House said Trump was warning of the risk of a nuclear Iran.
articles.byline: Jamie Whitehead & Bernd Debusmann Jr, White House reporter

blocks.text: Donald Trump's remark that Iran could "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego has sparked fierce backlash from California politicians - and a strongly worded rebuttal from the White House.

California Governor Gavin Newsom condemned the comment - made by Trump at an election campaign rally in Nebraska - as "deranged and dangerous," while LA Mayor Karen Bass described them as threats and an attempt to "encourage attacks on American lives".
According to the White House, however, Trump was saying that American cities would have been threatened by Iran had he not launched a war there earlier this year.
Both LA and San Diego house major US military installations including Navy ports and Air Force bases.

While speaking in Nebraska about the Iran conflict, he said: "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego."
There were cheers from sections of the audience as the comments about the two Californian cities were made.
San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria wrote that the city was not collateral damage in a post on X, while demanding Trump keep it out of his "reckless war talk".
In a second post on his official governor of California X account, Newsom shared an article on the comments from the Los Angeles Times saying it was "disgusting and disqualifying".
Trump is yet to respond to the statements made by California's leaders.
In a post on X, White House Communications Director Stephen Cheung described the "media freakout" over Trump's comments as "not rooted in reality".

"He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," Cheung wrote. "America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money".

The president and other administration officials often claim that disrupting Iran's nuclear programme was essential for US national security, and that any issues that have stemmed from the conflict were necessary.

A separate X post, from the official White House rapid response account, described journalists from the Los Angeles Times reporting on the comments as "buffoons" and again pushed back on the characterisation of the comments by Newsom and others.
"He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance," the account added.

San Diego, located 17 miles (27km) from the border with Mexico, is the eighth largest city in the US and is home to Naval Base San Diego, the home port of the US Navy's Pacific Fleet, and Naval Amphibious Base Coronado - the main training centre Navy Seals on the West Coast.
It is also where Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton is located, a base which 70,000 service members and civilians work at.
Located approximately 120 miles (193 KM) north of San Diego, Los Angeles is the second most populous city in the US.
It is home to the space system command headquarters of the US Space Force, as well as the Los Angeles Air Force Base.

articles.title: Spain court lifts Puigdemont arrest warrant, clearing way for his return home ahead of November elections
articles.summary: Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont fled Spain in 2017 after launching an independence bid. The court's decision means he can return home without fear of arrest after almost a decade in exile.

image.caption: The 63-year-old has been wanted by police since 2017Image: Glòria Sánchez/Europa Press/IMAGO

blocks.text: Spain's Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted an arrest warrant for Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, paving the way for him to return home ahead of a general election next month.
Puigdemont fled to Belgium in 2017 after leading a failed attempt for the wealthy northeastern Catalonia region to break away from Spain.
He had been wanted by authorities ever since, accused of embezzling public funds to hold an illegal independence referendum when he was head of Catalonia's regional government.
Judge Pablo Llarena lifted the arrest warrant shortly after Spain's Constitutional Court ruled that a 2024 amnesty for Catalan separatists also applied to embezzlement cases.
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez welcomed the decision, saying it would allow Catalonia to "look to the future."
"We should celebrate that this also helps Catalan society, as it has been demanding throughout this time," he told journalists in Madrid.
How did the amnesty come about?
While Puigdemont and other members of his government fled abroad after the 2017 independence bid, several Catalan ministers who remained in Spain were sentenced to lengthy prison terms.

In 2024, in the face of strong opposition from Spain's conservative and right-wing parties, the Sanchez government passed an amnesty law. It intended to cover all offenses related to the secession attempt and ease tensions in the Catalonia region.
It also allowed Sanchez to secure the backing of Catalan separatist parties and stay in power after a 2023 election produced no clear majority.
But Puigdemont's Junts party withdrew its support last year, accusing Sanchez of failing to fulfill promises such as providing amnesty for its leader.

Around 400 separatists have benefited from the amnesty, but Puigdemont had been excluded because Spain's Supreme Court initially ruled the law did not apply to those accused of embezzlement. That changed after the Constitutional Court on Tuesday sided with one of Puigdemont's allies who had appealed against the top court's ruling.
Last week, Junts voted against housing relief measures proposed by Sanchez's government amid huge protests, prompting the prime minister on Monday to call a snap vote for November 29.
Housing crisis triggers snap election in Spain

articles.title: Sara Duterte bank records submitted to impeachment court enjoy presumption of regularity
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday ruled that the bank records of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as submitted by the banks to the court, enjoy a presumption of…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 10:04pm

The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday ruled that the bank records of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as submitted by the banks to the court, enjoy a presumption of regularity.

Presiding officer Senator-Judge Escudero made the ruling after the defense team of the Vice President refused to stipulate, or agree, that the bank records submitted by the banks to the impeachment court are authentic.
This prompted the prosecution to present the bank officials to confirm the authenticity as well as the balance of the accounts under the names of the Vice President and her husband.

“To the extent that any record independently qualifies as an official record and is entitled to a presumption of regularity, that presumption is rebuttable and does not establish the truth or accuracy of every entry,” Escudero said during Day 34 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President.

Escudero said that this is in accordance with Rule 4, Section 1 of the Rules on Evidence which regards an electronic document as equivalent of an original under the original document rule when it is a printout of other or other output readable by site or other means and shown to reflect the data accurately.

“Upon a specific substantial showing of fraud, falsification, material alteration, irregularity, incompleteness, palpable mistake, unreliable method of preparation, a break in a chain of custody or lack of personal knowledge or material inconsistency with other evidence, the respondent or any other party may challenge the records admission, seek the exclusion or limitation of the disputed entries and request the appearance of appropriate custodian or other qualified witness as the case may be during cross examination or during the formal offer of evidence,” Escudero pointed out.

Escudero said this room for challenge is provided under Supreme Court decision on the Republic v. Marcos case under GR 171701 wherein the High Court ruled that the Presidential Commission on Good Government’s collection and custody of private documents did not convert them into public records or without more authenticate them particularly were only unauthenticated copies were presented.

“The court relies not on custody alone but the records, direct production by the institutional custodians pursuant to the subpoenas, their documented receipt and safe keeping by the clerk of court, their availability for inspection and their court's supervised reproduction,” Escudero said.

“We are not depriving the respondent of any of its available rights to question, the authenticity of the documents, but are simply trying to abbreviate the proceedings if there are no allegations nor claims of fraud, palpable mistake in the preparation of the documents in order to abbreviate the proceedings on these witnesses which are similarly situated,” Escudero added.

During the offer of evidence, private prosecutor James Alih told the Senate impeachment court said that the prosecution witness from the banks seeks to prove, among others, that the Vice President and her husband maintained 30 active bank accounts within 2022 to 2025 with a total ending balance of P190 million as of end of 2025.
This P190 million, Alih said, is not reflected in the Vice President’s SALN that she jointly filed with her husband since she did not declare any cash on hand or cash in bank from 2019 to 2025.

The absence of the Vice President’s declaration of cash in bank or cash on hand in her joint SALN with her husband were earlier testified to before the Senate impeachment court by Atty. Karen Batu of the Office of the Ombudsman.
On Tuesday, the prosecution was able to present two bank officials as witness namely:

items: Eunice Sumatra - Branch Head, LandBank San Pedro, Davao Branch
Raquel dela Cerna - Branch Manager, LandBank Davao Magsaysay Branch

blocks.text: Sumatra testified that the payroll account of the Vice President is an active account in their branch, while dela Cerna told the Senate impeachment court that Carpio had an ending balance of worth at least P1.3 million in his bank account in LandBank Davao Magsaysay Branch as of end of 2025. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecutor Ridon to VP Sara: 'Good luck'
articles.summary: “Good luck. Good luck to the Vice President. Because the end is near…the end is near, my friends, of the presentation of our evidence, just to be clear,” Rep. Terry Ridon said.

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 9:55pm

Representative Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list wished Vice President Sara Duterte "good luck," after she said he had a conflict of interest in his role as a House prosecutor in her impeachment trial.
“Good luck. Good luck to the Vice President. Because the end is near…the end is near, my friends, of the presentation of our evidence, just to be clear,” Ridon said on Tuesday.

Earlier that day, in a press conference in her hometown of Davao City, Duterte said Ridon had a conflict of interest because he used to be a consultant for the Davao city government’s anti-poverty initiatives.
Ridon disputed her claim of conflict of interest. saying that he was never a personal advisor to Duterte when she was the city's mayor.

“We performed the work required under the engagement and submitted the corresponding reports to the City Government. The consultancy was never subject to any audit disallowance, more than six years after the engagement concluded,” he said in a statement.

The prosecution is presenting evidence for Article 2 of the impeachment case against the Vice President, alleging unexplained wealth due to alleged failure to truthfully disclose assets in her SALN and failure to divest in businesses as required for the President and Vice President under a constitutional provision.
Ridon is one of the two lead prosecutors for Article 2 alongside Akbayan party-list Representative Chel Diokno.
“Tuloy-tuloy lang po kami. Wala po itong takot, wala itong pangamba. Tuloy-tuloy lang po ’yung paglalabas ng ebidensya ngayong linggo,” he said.
(We will soldier on. We are fearless and we have no doubts. Our presentation of evidence is unhampered.)

On Monday, Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura testified that there were P4.4 billion in covered and suspicious bank transactions recorded under the names of the Vice President and her husband Manases Carpio from 2007 to 2025.
Buenaventura also testified that Cale88 Foods Corp., which used to be one of the business interests of Carpio, also received P319.33 million in inward remittances from mainland China and Hong Kong.

On Tuesday, Buenaventura also said that the P319 million of onward remittances from mainland China and Hong Kong to Cale88 is part of the P1.2 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions recorded under Cale88 from 2022 to 2025.

Buenaventura also told the senator-judges that the three Cale88 transactions covering the P319-million remittance were reported as suspicious because there was “no underlying legal or trade obligation, purpose or economic justification.” — BM, GMA News

articles.title: As more Iranian women reject hijab rules, regime looks at new ways to force compliance
articles.summary: As more women in Iran reject Islamist rules on wearing hijab headscarves, hardliners are shifting focus from "morality police" street enforcement towards social pressure in workplaces, services and…

image.caption: Iran's regime pushes strict distinctions for women considered to be 'properly veiled' Image: Vahid Salemi/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Women appearing in public without wearing a hijab has become an increasingly common sight across Iran, marking one of the most visible social changes since the 2022 "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests, which were sparked after a woman died in police custody after she was arrested for allegedly wearing her headscarf improperly.

Authorities have been unable to restore the level of street enforcement that existed before the protests. But the relative retreat of so-called "morality police" patrols does not mean the compulsory hijab has disappeared.
Now, authorities and conservative groups are experimenting with different ways to resist that change without necessarily recreating the same street confrontations that helped fuel the 2022 protests.

Judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni-Ejei recently called for action against what he described as social "abnormalities," "indecency" and "nudity," urging prosecutors to coordinate with police, intelligence bodies and government institutions.

At the same time, supporters of hijab mandates have circulated online campaigns encouraging people to avoid businesses run by women who do not follow the state dress code and instead patronize women who do.
The result is a more fragmented form of enforcement, moving in some cases from police patrols toward workplaces, businesses and access to everyday services.
Iranian women unveiled: A shift in hijab enforcement?
Iran's regime turns to social pressure
The online campaigns call for what supporters describe as "conscious purchasing," encouraging consumers to support hijab-observing vendors.
A female lawyer in Tehran told DW that such campaigns risk deepening social divisions rather than encouraging adherence to a social norm.
"This is a deliberate attempt to categorize people by identity and put them against one another," she said under condition of anonymity for safety concerns.
She argues that encouraging economic pressure against people solely because of their appearance goes beyond an individual's right to choose where to shop.

"When economic sanctions are imposed on them [the regime], they call it pressure, injustice and economic warfare," she said. "But when they use the same logic domestically to force part of society to change its behavior, it becomes 'support for values.'"
She also questioned the assumption that women who conform to one particular dress code uniquely represent Iranian social values.
"The reality of Iranian society is much more complex than that," she said.

Accounts posted by Iranian women suggest that dress-code enforcement can also appear in everyday services, with some women reporting on social media being denied access to clinics and banks for not wearing a headscarf.

blocks.caption: The death 22-year-old Jina Mahsa Amini in 2022 symbolized the Iranian regime's oppression of womenImage: UGC

blocks.text: When women's bodies become political
Shirin Shams is an exiled Iranian political activist and director of the Women's Revolution Organization, which advocates for secularism, women's liberation, and human rights in Iran.
She told DW the recent campaigns targeting women who ditch the compulsory hijab are an attempt to revive social divisions that were weakened during the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement.
"The Islamic Republic has tried for years to divide women according to their clothing," the Germany-based activist said.

She describes the compulsory hijab as one of the Iranian state's most important ideological lines and argues that the widespread presence of women without headscarves shows how far social reality has moved beyond official expectations.
The renewed campaigns, in her view, are about more than clothing, representing an effort to reconstruct a boundary between women who comply and those who do not.
Saeed Paivandi, a professor at the University of Lorraine in France, says the conflict reflects a broader struggle over social control.
He told DW that Iranian authorities have spent years creating distinctions between women considered properly veiled and those officially labeled "badly veiled" or "unveiled."
"The government is once again turning women's bodies into a social, moral and even security issue," Peyvandi said.

A woman without a headscarf is not interpreted merely as someone making an individual choice, he said. For parts of the political establishment, she can also represent a visible challenge to an ideological order.
'I will be living proof of the violent oppression in Iran'
Iran's hardliners vs. modern reality

While Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has repeatedly spoken about social cohesion and national unity, conservative Islamist judicial and political figures continue to demand tougher enforcement of dress regulations.
This produces an uneasy balance and exposes differences within Iran's political establishment.

Parts of the establishment appear aware that a return to large-scale confrontations between police and women could carry significant social and political costs. Others are unwilling to accept the normalization of women appearing in public without wearing a hijab.
The result is neither the old system of comprehensive street enforcement nor an end to compulsory dress rules.
Instead, pressure can appear intermittently through courts, workplaces, businesses, administrative procedures and social campaigns.

blocks.caption: In 2022, protests erupted across Iran after a woman died in the custody of the 'morality police"Image: AFP

blocks.text: Enforcement without the 'morality police'
Paivandi believes direct coercion has reached its limits and that supporters of Islamic dress codes are looking for alternative ways to enforce conformity.
That could shift part of the burden from state institutions to society itself.
A bank employee, clinic receptionist, employer, shopkeeper or customer can become involved in enforcing standards even without a police officer being present.
This makes the boundary between law, personal discretion and ideological pressure increasingly unclear.
Peyvandi also warns that linking religion to humiliation, exclusion and coercion could further alienate younger Iranians from religious institutions.
Women who choose to wear a hijab may also be drawn into a confrontation they did not choose, he said, if their clothing is presented as a marker of political loyalty.

articles.title: Southeast Asia's haze crisis: Have lessons been learned?
articles.summary: Eleven years after catastrophic fires prompted promises of tougher action, Southeast Asia is again choking on transboundary haze, raising questions about whether the region has learned the lessons of…

image.caption: Indonesia's long 2026 dry season, coupled with this year's El Nino, has worsened what has become an almost annual crisisImage: Willy Kurniawan/REUTERS

blocks.text: Indonesia's worst wildfire season in more than a decade is exposing how much, and how little, Southeast Asia's response to haze has changed since 2015.

Forest and land fires have burned across parts of the Indonesian islands of Sumatra, Borneo and Papua for weeks, sending smoke across large areas of the country and into neighboring Malaysia and Singapore.

Indonesia's long 2026 dry season, coupled with this year's El Nino, has worsened what has become an almost annual crisis, exposing millions of people to hazardous smoke containing harmful microscopic particles.

More than 170,000 cases of acute respiratory infection were recorded in haze-affected areas of Indonesia between August and mid-September, according to the country's Health Ministry, including more than 40,000 cases involving young children.
The haze has forced hundreds of schools to close in Malaysia and pushed more than 1.4 million Indonesian students into remote learning, although the full economic cost is not yet known.

blocks.caption: The haze has spread to Malaysia and forced hundreds of schools to closeImage: Arif Kartono/AFP

blocks.text: Will severe haze become more frequent?

This year's severe weather is only part of the explanation. Fire has long been used as a cheap way to clear land for agriculture in Southeast Asia, while the expansion of palm oil and pulpwood plantations has drained and degraded large areas of peatland.

The echoes of 2015 are hard to ignore. That year's fires burned roughly 2.6 million hectares of land, produced months of severe haze across Southeast Asia and cost Indonesia an estimated $16 billion (€14.2 billion) in economic losses, according to the World Bank.
The risk is growing that severe haze will become more frequent as climate conditions worsen, Paruedee Nguitragool, an associate professor at Chiang Mai University in Thailand, told DW.
"Haze, which used to be mainly a problem in maritime Southeast Asia, has become a concern for most countries in the region," she added.
Governments within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), the regional bloc, "need to be more open to one another and work closely together."
"Farmers and companies need alternative methods of land clearing and incentives to adopt them, while land and forest rehabilitation must also be implemented," Nguitragool said.
"At the same time, consumers need to be more aware of whether the products they buy come from sustainable practices and whether burning was involved in their production," she added.

blocks.caption: Fire has long been used as a cheap way to clear land for agriculture in Southeast AsiaImage: Reina/AFP

blocks.text: What changed after 2015?

The 2015 disaster triggered major policy changes. Indonesia strengthened peatland restoration, fire monitoring, enforcement and firefighting, while ASEAN expanded regional cooperation, David Mark Taylor, a professor of tropical environmental change at the National University of Singapore, told DW.

Indonesia established the Peatland Restoration Agency in 2016 to restore millions of hectares of degraded peat. Its mandate was later expanded to mangrove rehabilitation, with the agency renamed the Peatland and Mangrove Restoration Agency.
A permanent moratorium on new concessions in primary forests and peatlands also restricted further development in some vulnerable areas.

Authorities have also increasingly pursued companies in court. Last year, an appeals court ordered palm oil company PT Banyu Kahuripan Indonesia to pay around €14 million in environmental damages over fires covering more than 3,300 hectares of its concession. Other companies have faced much tougher restoration orders.

At the regional level, ASEAN adopted a new Peatland Management Strategy and a second Haze-Free Roadmap for 2023-2030, and the long-awaited ASEAN Coordinating Center for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control opened its secretariat in Jakarta in April, more than two decades after the 2002 ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution.
"But the underlying problem hasn't gone away, and neither has the driver," said Taylor.

Extensive areas of peat remain drained or degraded, including cleared land that has yet to be put into productive use. Such poorly managed or "idle" peatlands can become highly combustible during prolonged drought, Taylor noted.
There is also disagreement over how much restoration Indonesia has actually achieved.

The Peatland and Mangrove Restoration Agency ceased operating at the end of 2024, with its responsibilities returned to other government ministries and institutions, raising questions among environmentalists about whether they can maintain the same institutional focus.

ASEAN faces its own limitations. Its 2002 haze agreement is legally binding, but many targets and implementation plans depend on national governments acting on them. The regional bloc has few mechanisms to compel governments to meet those targets or punish failure.
But the ultimate driver for all of this "is the global demand for cheap, plantation-grown commodities, such as palm oil and pulp and paper, which most of us are responsible for," said Taylor.
"So long as that demand persists, so too will the pressure to convert peatlands and forests to plantations," he added.
Indonesia's battle with slash and burn farming
Can ASEAN stop the next crisis?
This year's fires have turned attention from creating new agreements to how Southeast Asian governments can make existing mechanisms work.

"To prevent this from worsening further, there needs to be a real pooling of capacity among ASEAN. Indonesia, for all its efforts, does not have the capacity to manage it alone," Helena Varkkey, an associate professor at Universiti Malaya, told DW.

The existing ASEAN mechanisms for joint emergency response should be operationalized, she added, but this should have been arranged before the start of the haze season, as meteorological reports made it clear that a "Super El Nino" was comingearlier this year.

"Southeast Asian governments need to work together to prevent biomass-burning episodes by implementing stringent laws to stop peat and forest fires. They need to use all available technologies together to prepare for dry conditions," Mohd Talib Latif, a professor at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, told DW.
"Haze needs to be considered a disaster for this region," he added.

articles.title: N.L. spent millions renovating old college for future courthouse — now it's slated for demolition
articles.summary: After pausing work at the Martin Gallant Building in Stephenville Crossing this past summer, the Newfoundland and Labrador government says the building needs to be demolished, axing plans for it to…

blocks.text: Nfld. & Labrador

After pausing work at the Martin Gallant Building in Stephenville Crossing this past summer, the Newfoundland and Labrador government says the building needs to be demolished, axing plans for it to become the new courthouse and provincial government services building. Mayor Lisa Lucas is now worried about what it means for her community.
Stephenville Crossing mayor says she's worried about future of her community
Teardown order concerns Stephenville Crossing mayor
After millions of dollars were spent redeveloping an old college building on Newfoundland’s west coast, the Newfoundland and Labrador government says it’s now set to be torn down.

In June, the province announced it was pausing work at the Martin Gallant building in Stephenville Crossing after spending $5.6 million. It was once home to the College of the North Atlantic and was planned to be the new courthouse and provincial government services building in the community.

On Monday, the provincial Department of Transportation and Infrastructure said following additional environmental and structural assessments, it had been determined the building needed to be demolished.
Stephenville Crossing Mayor Lisa Lucas says the decision has her worried about the future of her community.
"The current premier wants to go down in history as being the person that signed our community's death warrant," Lucas told CBC Radio’s Newfoundland Morning.
"I'm not going to be surprised if six months from now or seven months from now the PC government announces the new courthouse is going up in Stephenville."

In its statement, the department said further investigation showed the project would be significantly more complex and expensive than previously anticipated. It also pointed to the presence of contaminated soil, lead paint and structural deficiencies.
Lucas said she wants the province to act quickly to demolish the site, citing safety concerns.
"We want that down, and we want it down now if they're deeming it — this— unsafe."
She called the site a "prime piece of real estate" and wonders what will happen to it now.
Residents were previously excited when plans to redevelop the building for government services were announced by the previous Liberal government — which has now turned to fear, she said.

In the past, Lucas said the town has had a good relationship with the region's MHA, regardless of political party, but it seems there’s a lack of transparency and communication with the PC government.
The previous Liberal government had started renovating the Martin Gallant Building after concerns were raised about the accessibility of the provincial building in nearby Stephenville.

In a previous statement to Radio-Canada, a Department of Transportation spokesperson said the government had previously estimated the redevelopment would only cost $8 million. But after work started, the price tag went up, and in May 2025 a $28.6-million contract was awarded.

The statement went on to say the most recent cost projections went up to $40 million, and the contractor raised concerns about "significant challenges" due to only having a "partial design" at the time of tender.
'A fiasco'
Speaking at an unrelated announcement in Corner Brook Tuesday morning, Wakeham called the project “a fiasco,” pointing to how the project's price tag ballooned.
“And then we now find out that there were structural issues with it and the grounds contaminated,” Wakeham told reporters.
He said they have to figure out if the site can be used for any other purpose in the future.
“My minister will be reaching out to communities and we’ll look at where we go in terms of future developments,” said Wakeham.
Premier Tony Wakeham says given the state of the site, they have to figure out if it can be used for any other purpose in the future. (Amy Feehan/CBC)
'Serious concerns'
Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure Barry Petten is expected to speak with CBC News Wednesday in an interview.

items: After spending $5.6M, N.L. hits pause on Stephenville Crossing courthouse development
Roughly $2.6M spent on Cartwright school before N.L. government halted project

blocks.text: In Monday’s statement, Petten said upon review of the redevelopment, there were "serious concerns" over its feasibility and cost, adding further review has highlighted problems with the project that should have been known before it was undertaken.

"Had these conditions been identified and assessed earlier in the process, the scope, cost and viability of the project could have been more accurately evaluated from the outset," Petten said in the statement.
"While this is disappointing news, it would not be responsible to continue pursuing a project that no longer represents a sound investment of public funds."
The government is assessing other available spaces in the region for government services.

articles.title: Defence lawyer in Cornell University case calls for special prosecutor to be removed
articles.summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James is investigating the rape allegations, but the lawyer says comments she made on the case should disqualify her.

blocks.text: A lawyer for one of the seven men accused of participating in a Cornell University gang rape has called for the special prosecutor on the case to recuse herself over past public comments.
The lawyer had said a social post from New York Attorney General Letitia James throws into question her investigation's "integrity and independence".
In the 28 September post, James wrote that "what this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable" and told survivors that "we stand with you".
The university's administration is under fire over its alleged mishandling of the October 2024 incident and, according to US media, now faces a no-confidence vote by Cornell faculty.
The university's Faculty Senate, a governing body comprised of professors and other academic staff, will vote on a resolution of no confidence next week, according to reports.
A majority no-confidence vote would be a largely symbolic gesture, signalling the broader faculty's discontent and applying pressure on university leadership to act.
The BBC has reached out to Cornell University for comment.

Allegations made in a lawsuit against seven men and the university have rocked the campus in New York state, with hundreds of students and faculty members gathering there on Monday in protest, and sparked anger across the country.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul last week appointed James as a special prosecutor to investigate the case and how law enforcement and the university initially responded to the allegations made by a woman identified in the lawsuit as Jane Doe.
Jane Doe has accused the university of failing to protect her, after she was allegedly drugged and raped by the men for several hours at a fraternity party.
Days before she was appointed special prosecutor, James wrote on X: "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable.
"I'm holding her in my heart and in my prayers," she continued. "To her, and to all survivors: you're not alone. We stand with you."
The lawyer for one of the seven accused said these remarks were disqualifying.
In a statement sent to the BBC's US media partner, CBS News, the lawyer said her comments conflict with the need for "independently evaluating the evidence".
"This is not an accusation that Attorney General James is corrupt, acting in bad faith or incapable of performing her duties professionally," the statement said.

"Nor am I suggesting that a court has determined that she is legally disqualified. The point is much narrower: an avoidable question now hangs over this investigation, and voluntary recusal would remove it."
Governor Hochul and James were questioned about impartiality concerns during a news conference, and Hochul said James would "follow the facts".
"She'll examine the evidence and go wherever it leads, and if the evidence supports charges, she will pursue them," Hochul said.

articles.title: Canada's trade surplus widens to more than 4-year high in August, as front-loading ramps up
articles.summary: Canada's trade surplus with the U.S. hit a 19-month high in August, Statistics Canada reported on Tuesday.

image.caption: Transport trucks are seen in Aulac, N.B. (CBC)

blocks.text: Business·New
Canada's trade surplus with the U.S. hit a 19-month high in August, Statistics Canada reported on Tuesday.
Exporters shipped more to ​the U.S. to beat looming 50% tariffs from ​Trump administration

Canada's trade surplus widened substantially in August to $4.2 billion, data showed on Tuesday, as exporters rushed to increase shipments to the U.S. before President Donald Trump's new tariffs took effect.
Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast the trade surplus would expand to $1.55 billion, from an upwardly revised $787 million.

As exporters shipped more to ​the U.S. to beat the looming 50 per cent tariffs, Canada's exports stateside surged 8.1 per cent in August, while imports from the U.S. were down 2.5 per cent, Statistics Canada reported.

This change helped Canada post a trade surplus with the ​U.S. of $11.2 billion, a 19-month high, lifting its share of exports to its biggest ⁠trading partner to almost ⁠70 per cent for the first time since September 2025.
Trump's new ‌tariffs, which cover roughly $20 billion of Canadian exports to the U.S., came into effect on Aug. 22.

Economists have said that September would show a more accurate impact of the new tariffs, which apply to a variety of items, including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods ⁠and hockey equipment.
September will also show the impact of Canadian counter-tariffs on U.S. imports and Trump's ban on some goods imports from Canada.
Canada's overall exports increased by 2.5 per cent in August to $77.91 billion, after falling by 2.6 per cent ‌in the previous month.

Exports of energy products — refined petroleum products and crude oil — posted the biggest overall gain, increasing by 4.7 per cent to $19.03 billion. A stronger Canadian dollar also affected the value of exports.
Consumer goods, machinery exports up
Excluding energy products, exports were up 1.8 per cent. In volume terms, total exports rose 2.5 per cent, StatsCan ​said.

Exports of consumer goods were up 6.6 per cent, industrial machinery, equipment and parts were up 10.1 per cent and electronic and electrical equipment and parts increased 11 per cent ⁠in August, the statistics agency said.
Imports were down two per cent to $73.71 billion, with imports of motor vehicles and ⁠parts posting the largest decline in August.

As Canada negotiated waves of tariffs across some crucial sectors ⁠such ⁠as steel, aluminum, autos and lumber for ​almost 18 months, its export dependence on the U.S. had shrunk, while exports to the rest of the world ​rose, as it sought to ⁠diversify its trade partners.

After increasing 8.2 per cent in July, exports to countries other than the U.S. fell 8.5 per cent in August, and imports decreased. Its trade deficit with countries other than the U.S. widened to $7 billion in August from $5.3 billion in July, StatsCan said.
The Canadian dollar strengthened after the trade data, with the currency trading up 0.05 per cent ⁠to $1.4250 to the U.S. dollar, or ‌70.18 U.S. cents.
